Systematic refactoring of the workspace-hub repo ecosystem, starting with tier-1 repositories. The goal is to reduce architectural debt, consolidate duplicate patterns, enforce consistent structure, and improve agent navigability across all tier-1 repos.

## Tier-1 Repos (Priority Order)

| # | Repo | Purpose | Maturity | Depends On |
|---|------|---------|----------|------------|
| 1 | `digitalmodel/` | Engineering digital twin (asset integrity, CP, GIS, hydro) | beta | assetutilities |
| 2 | `assetutilities/` | Shared engineering utilities (config, units, calculations) | stable | — |
| 3 | `assethold/` | Asset portfolio financial analysis | beta | assetutilities |
| 4 | `worldenergydata/` | Global energy market data (BSEE, EIA, drilling) | beta | assetutilities |
| 5 | `CAD-DEVELOPMENTS/` | CAD solvers, models, database, utilities | beta | — |
| 6 | `aceengineer-website/` | Consulting website | — | — |
| 7 | `aceengineer-strategy/` | GTM, business strategy | — | — |
| 8 | `sabithaandkrishnaestates/` | SKEstates Inc. business ops | — | — |

## Refactoring Scope

### Phase 1: Audit (analysis-only, no code changes)
- [ ] Run `repo-architecture-analysis` on each tier-1 repo
- [ ] Identify cross-repo duplicate code (especially assetutilities consumers)
- [ ] Map dependency graph (imports, shared configs, data flows)
- [ ] Catalog test coverage per repo (current state)
- [ ] Identify orphaned/dead code, unused modules, oversized files (>400 lines)
- [ ] Score each repo against the Control-Plane Contract (AGENTS.md, provider adapters)
- [ ] Identify skill duplicates across repos (134 known from vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1720 audit)

### Phase 2: Plan (per-repo refactor plans)
- [ ] Generate refactor plan per tier-1 repo with estimated effort
- [ ] Prioritize by: business value × technical debt severity × dependency impact
- [ ] Identify breaking changes and migration paths
- [ ] Define test coverage targets (tier-1 = 85% per pytest.tier1.ini)

### Phase 3: Execute (TDD, incremental, per-repo)
- [ ] Execute refactors repo-by-repo following dependency order (assetutilities first)
- [ ] TDD mandatory — tests before implementation
- [ ] Each repo refactor as a separate sub-issue for tracking

## Execution Strategy: Claude Code Plan Mode (Cloud)

### Claude Code `--permission-mode plan` ("Ultraplan")

Claude Code v2.1.92 supports `--permission-mode plan` which restricts the agent to **read-only analysis and planning** — no file writes, no shell mutations. This is ideal for Phase 1 (Audit) and Phase 2 (Plan).

**Proposed execution:**

```bash
# Phase 1: Audit each tier-1 repo in plan mode (safe, read-only)
claude --permission-mode plan \
  --print \
  --model claude-opus-4-6 \
  --max-budget-usd 5 \
  -p "Audit the repository architecture of digitalmodel/. Analyze: module structure, dependency graph, test coverage, dead code, file sizes >400 lines, AGENTS.md compliance. Output a structured JSON report."

# Phase 2: Generate refactor plan
claude --permission-mode plan \
  --print \
  --model claude-opus-4-6 \
  --max-budget-usd 5 \
  -p "Given the audit report, generate a prioritized refactor plan for digitalmodel/. Include: breaking changes, migration steps, test targets, estimated effort per module."
```

### Cloud Execution Considerations

| Aspect | Status | Notes |
|--------|--------|-------|
| **Claude Code CLI** | Installed (v2.1.92) | Available on ace-linux-1 |
| **Plan mode** | Supported | `--permission-mode plan` — read-only, safe for audit |
| **API-key mode** | Supported | `--bare` + `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for headless/cloud runs |
| **Print mode** | Supported | `-p` / `--print` for non-interactive batch execution |
| **Budget cap** | Supported | `--max-budget-usd` to control spend per run |
| **Cloud sandbox** | Possible | Can run via Hermes `delegate_task` with `acp_command='claude'` |
| **Max subscription** | Claude Max $200/mo | Rate-limited but sufficient for plan-mode audit |

### Recommended Approach
1. **Phase 1 + 2 (Audit + Plan)**: Run Claude Code in plan mode via `delegate_task(acp_command='claude')` — subagents get isolated context, read-only, budget-capped
2. **Phase 3 (Execute)**: Requires interactive Claude Code sessions with full permissions — NOT suited for autonomous cloud execution without user oversight

## Adversarial Review Requirements

Per [AI Review Routing Policy](docs/standards/AI_REVIEW_ROUTING_POLICY.md):

- **3-agent adversarial review at BOTH stages** (plan + code/artifact)
- Claude: orchestrator + reviewer
- Codex: implementation worker + adversarial reviewer
- Gemini: architecture reviewer + adversarial reviewer
- Max 3 review iterations per deliverable
- All MAJOR findings must be resolved before completion

### Review Checkpoints
1. **After Phase 1 (Audit)**: All 3 agents review the audit findings
2. **After Phase 2 (Plan)**: All 3 agents review each repo's refactor plan
3. **After Phase 3 (Execute)**: All 3 agents review code changes per repo

Cross-agent confirmation across 9 independent passes makes this a high-confidence, reproducible defect — not a sampling artifact.

## Defects

### 1. Missing organization buckets in classifier enum

### 2. Unknown-bucket pollution (n=629)
Sampling the 629-doc Unknown bucket shows it is dominated by ASME B16/B31 codes and ASCE-7 standards that should reclassify cleanly to their proper publisher once #1 is fixed.

### 3. Personal-document misfiling into ISO (~196 of 308)
~196 of 308 ISO-tagged docs are personal/legal correspondence (BVI legal letters, bank correspondence, etc.) accidentally tagged as ISO. **Real ISO standards population is ~112 docs** — i.e. the ISO bucket is ~64% noise.

20 of 80 BSI-tagged docs are misclassified: 4 ABS Guide PDFs, 11 FAOS joint-industry publications, 7 generic `Corrigenda.pdf` / `RCN1.pdf` files.

Surfaced during [#2616](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2616). Two tests in \`tests/contracts/\` fail in the full suite but pass in isolation — classic test-pollution Heisenbug, made deterministic by \`-p no:randomly\`.

## Defect

- \`tests/contracts/test_assetutilities_common_contract.py::test_update_deep_dictionary_importable\` → \`AssertionError: <MagicMock> == 1\`
- \`tests/contracts/test_assetutilities_data_contract.py::test_AttributeDict_importable\` → \`AssertionError: <MagicMock> == 'value'\`

## Root cause

Some upstream test in the suite registers \`assetutilities.common.update_deep\` and \`assetutilities.common.data\` (or similar \`assetutilities.*\` modules) as \`MagicMock()\` in \`sys.modules\` without restoring them. With \`-p no:randomly\` the ordering is deterministic, so the pollution is reproducible. When the contract tests later import the real symbols they receive the mock.

## Verification

\`pytest tests/contracts/\` in isolation → **17/17 pass**. Sibling repo \`../assetutilities/src/assetutilities/common/update_deep.py\` carries both \`update_deep_dictionary\` and \`AttributeDict\` correctly.

For a given property, build a GIS-based timeline showing how the surrounding area has developed over time and project how future development may evolve. ## Proposal: Hermes-Orchestrated Workflow with Hard Stops

### Phase 1: Session Lifecycle Gates

**Mandatory User Hard Stops (cannot be bypassed):**

```
SESSION START
  ├─ [GATE 1: Session Init] Auto — load context, check prior state, validate env
  │
  ├─ [GATE 2: Work Selection] Auto — triage issues, present options
  │
  ├─ [HARD STOP 1: Plan Approval] ◆ USER MUST APPROVE plan before any implementation
  │
  ├─ [GATE 3: TDD Red] Auto — tests written, all failing (enforced, not advisory)
  │
  ├─ [GATE 4: Implementation] Auto — make tests pass
  │
  ├─ [GATE 5: Cross-Review] Auto — route to Codex+Gemini per routing policy
  │
  ├─ [HARD STOP 2: Review Verdict] ◆ USER REVIEWS cross-review results, approves/rejects
  │
  ├─ [GATE 6: Commit+Push] Auto — commit, push, close issue
  │
  └─ [HARD STOP 3: Session Close] ◆ USER CONFIRMS session summary, next priorities
SESSION END
```

3 hard stops per session. Everything else is automated by Hermes.

### Phase 2: Runaway Protection

- **Tool-call ceiling**: Auto-pause at 200 tool calls, require user confirmation to continue
- **Time ceiling**: Auto-pause after 45 minutes of continuous work, present progress summary
- **Error loop breaker**: If same error repeats 3x, hard stop — do not retry
- **Credit guard**: Pause if estimated session cost exceeds threshold (ties to #1838)

- Create `cross-review-policy` skill (policy exists as doc, not as actionable skill)

### Phase 4: Hermes as Workflow Orchestrator

Hermes (not Claude Code directly) orchestrates the session lifecycle:
- Hermes manages gate transitions and hard-stop enforcement
- Hermes dispatches to Claude/Codex/Gemini per routing matrix (#1838)
- Hermes tracks session metrics (tool calls, time, credits, gate pass/fail)
- Hermes generates session report at close (ties to gsd-session-report)
- Inter-session continuity: Hermes checks last session state before starting new work

## Summary
Standardize the canonical OpenFOAM baseline for portable engineering work, using repo-tracked docs, scripts, example cases, and validation.

Part of #1782.
Primary reference: #25.
Supports downstream work such as #1268.

## Motivation
OpenFOAM is already CLI-native, but the baseline workflow is not yet fully encoded as a portable artifact bundle. We need a declared version target, canonical entrypoints, and a smoke validation path.

## Scope
Create the baseline OpenFOAM portability package in workspace-hub.

Expected deliverables:
- baseline docs
- run/validation entrypoints
- minimal smoke example
- troubleshooting guidance
- shared skill update if reusable guidance is improved

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] baseline doc declares the target fork/version explicitly (default: ESI/OpenFOAM.com v2312 unless changed by decision)
- [ ] canonical runner command(s) are documented
- [ ] minimal smoke case exists under a reproducible repo-tracked path
- [ ] validator produces pass/fail output with explicit checks
- [ ] common failure modes and version/fork mismatches are documented
- [ ] workflow can be executed on the canonical engineering host with documented prerequisites

## Notes
Implementation should prefer:
- explicit version detection and fail-fast behavior
- repo-tracked wrappers over tribal command memory
- logs/results/validation outputs in predictable locations

issues.title: FEATURE: Tier-1 Repo Ecosystem Refactoring — audit, plan, execute with Claude Code plan mode
issues.body:
## Summary

Systematic refactoring of the workspace-hub repo ecosystem, starting with tier-1 repositories. The goal is to reduce architectural debt, consolidate duplicate patterns, enforce consistent structure, and improve agent navigability across all tier-1 repos.

## Tier-1 Repos (Priority Order)

| # | Repo | Purpose | Maturity | Depends On |
|---|------|---------|----------|------------|
| 1 | `digitalmodel/` | Engineering digital twin (asset integrity, CP, GIS, hydro) | beta | assetutilities |
| 2 | `assetutilities/` | Shared engineering utilities (config, units, calculations) | stable | — |
| 3 | `assethold/` | Asset portfolio financial analysis | beta | assetutilities |
| 4 | `worldenergydata/` | Global energy market data (BSEE, EIA, drilling) | beta | assetutilities |
| 5 | `CAD-DEVELOPMENTS/` | CAD solvers, models, database, utilities | beta | — |
| 6 | `aceengineer-website/` | Consulting website | — | — |
| 7 | `aceengineer-strategy/` | GTM, business strategy | — | — |
| 8 | `sabithaandkrishnaestates/` | SKEstates Inc. business ops | — | — |

## Refactoring Scope

### Phase 1: Audit (analysis-only, no code changes)
- [ ] Run `repo-architecture-analysis` on each tier-1 repo
- [ ] Identify cross-repo duplicate code (especially assetutilities consumers)
- [ ] Map dependency graph (imports, shared configs, data flows)
- [ ] Catalog test coverage per repo (current state)
- [ ] Identify orphaned/dead code, unused modules, oversized files (>400 lines)
- [ ] Score each repo against the Control-Plane Contract (AGENTS.md, provider adapters)
- [ ] Identify skill duplicates across repos (134 known from vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1720 audit)

### Phase 2: Plan (per-repo refactor plans)
- [ ] Generate refactor plan per tier-1 repo with estimated effort
- [ ] Prioritize by: business value × technical debt severity × dependency impact
- [ ] Identify breaking changes and migration paths
- [ ] Define test coverage targets (tier-1 = 85% per pytest.tier1.ini)

### Phase 3: Execute (TDD, incremental, per-repo)
- [ ] Execute refactors repo-by-repo following dependency order (assetutilities first)
- [ ] TDD mandatory — tests before implementation
- [ ] Each repo refactor as a separate sub-issue for tracking

## Execution Strategy: Claude Code Plan Mode (Cloud)

### Claude Code `--permission-mode plan` ("Ultraplan")

Claude Code v2.1.92 supports `--permission-mode plan` which restricts the agent to **read-only analysis and planning** — no file writes, no shell mutations. This is ideal for Phase 1 (Audit) and Phase 2 (Plan).

**Proposed execution:**

```bash
# Phase 1: Audit each tier-1 repo in plan mode (safe, read-only)
claude --permission-mode plan \
  --print \
  --model claude-opus-4-6 \
  --max-budget-usd 5 \
  -p "Audit the repository architecture of digitalmodel/. Analyze: module structure, dependency graph, test coverage, dead code, file sizes >400 lines, AGENTS.md compliance. Output a structured JSON report."

# Phase 2: Generate refactor plan
claude --permission-mode plan \
  --print \
  --model claude-opus-4-6 \
  --max-budget-usd 5 \
  -p "Given the audit report, generate a prioritized refactor plan for digitalmodel/. Include: breaking changes, migration steps, test targets, estimated effort per module."
```

### Cloud Execution Considerations

| Aspect | Status | Notes |
|--------|--------|-------|
| **Claude Code CLI** | Installed (v2.1.92) | Available on ace-linux-1 |
| **Plan mode** | Supported | `--permission-mode plan` — read-only, safe for audit |
| **API-key mode** | Supported | `--bare` + `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for headless/cloud runs |
| **Print mode** | Supported | `-p` / `--print` for non-interactive batch execution |
| **Budget cap** | Supported | `--max-budget-usd` to control spend per run |
| **Cloud sandbox** | Possible | Can run via Hermes `delegate_task` with `acp_command='claude'` |
| **Max subscription** | Claude Max $200/mo | Rate-limited but sufficient for plan-mode audit |

### Recommended Approach
1. **Phase 1 + 2 (Audit + Plan)**: Run Claude Code in plan mode via `delegate_task(acp_command='claude')` — subagents get isolated context, read-only, budget-capped
2. **Phase 3 (Execute)**: Requires interactive Claude Code sessions with full permissions — NOT suited for autonomous cloud execution without user oversight

## Adversarial Review Requirements

Per [AI Review Routing Policy](docs/standards/AI_REVIEW_ROUTING_POLICY.md):

- **3-agent adversarial review at BOTH stages** (plan + code/artifact)
- Claude: orchestrator + reviewer
- Codex: implementation worker + adversarial reviewer
- Gemini: architecture reviewer + adversarial reviewer
- Max 3 review iterations per deliverable
- All MAJOR findings must be resolved before completion

### Review Checkpoints
1. **After Phase 1 (Audit)**: All 3 agents review the audit findings
2. **After Phase 2 (Plan)**: All 3 agents review each repo's refactor plan
3. **After Phase 3 (Execute)**: All 3 agents review code changes per repo

## Related Issues
- vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1567 — Feature: Continuous Repo Architecture Intelligence
- vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1545 — Agentic feature progression for repo ecosystem productivity under GSD
- vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1603 — Multi-repo architecture scan — expand scanner to all tier-1 repos

issues.title: O&G-Standards consolidator: 8 catalog-classification defects surfaced by parallel-agent ingest
issues.body:
## Summary

Iterations 8-9 of the LLM-wiki completeness loop ran 9 parallel research agents against `/mnt/ace/O&G-Standards/`. They independently surfaced the same structural classification gap in the upstream **O&G Standards Consolidation System** (per `_catalog.json` `metadata.source`, version 1.0.0, generated 2025-12-25). The consolidator's outputs — `_catalog.json` (19.5 MB), `_inventory.db` (6.8 GB SQLite), `_catalog.html` — encode the eight defects below, which all downstream wiki ingest, retrieval, and citation consumers inherit.

Cross-agent confirmation across 9 independent passes makes this a high-confidence, reproducible defect — not a sampling artifact.

Session log with full iteration history: [docs/sessions/2026-05-08-llm-wiki-completeness-loop.md](../blob/main/docs/sessions/2026-05-08-llm-wiki-completeness-loop.md)

## Defects

### 1. Missing organization buckets in classifier enum
`_catalog.json` `statistics.by_organization` enumerates only ASTM / Unknown / API / ISO / DNV / OnePetro / BSI / Norsok / MIL / NEMA / SNAME. **ABS, ASCE, ASME, AWS, NACE, IEC, HSE are absent from the enum** despite having on-disk folders (ABS / 29 PDFs, ASME / 88, AWS / 15, etc.). Their docs spill into the Unknown bucket or adjacent publishers.

### 2. Unknown-bucket pollution (n=629)
Sampling the 629-doc Unknown bucket shows it is dominated by ASME B16/B31 codes and ASCE-7 standards that should reclassify cleanly to their proper publisher once #1 is fixed.

### 3. Personal-document misfiling into ISO (~196 of 308)
~196 of 308 ISO-tagged docs are personal/legal correspondence (BVI legal letters, bank correspondence, etc.) accidentally tagged as ISO. **Real ISO standards population is ~112 docs** — i.e. the ISO bucket is ~64% noise.

### 4. BSI bucket impurity ~25% (20 of 80)
20 of 80 BSI-tagged docs are misclassified: 4 ABS Guide PDFs, 11 FAOS joint-industry publications, 7 generic `Corrigenda.pdf` / `RCN1.pdf` files.

### 5. API structural-fragment artefacts (n=125)
125 docs in API are page-fragments (`Sect_*`, `append_*`, `Page-NN-Metric-Table`) inflating the Unclassified sub-bucket. These appear to be PDF-extraction debris that was indexed as standalone docs.

### 6. ASTM cross-series misfiling (~1,000+)
Across A/D/E/G-Series boundaries: 190 misfiled in A, 121 in D, several in E, 9 in G. C/B/F-committee codes are scattered across a top-level loose bucket rather than routed to their committee folders.

### 7. Filename quality degraded (54.7% of ASTM top-level loose)
54.7% of ASTM top-level loose docs carry corrupted base64-ish trailing tokens (e.g. `_QJMYNW_`), likely PDF-metadata-extraction artifacts that bled into filenames.

### 8. OCR coverage <1% on ASTM
Only **71 OCR text files for 18,000+ ASTM PDFs** — full-text retrieval is effectively unavailable for the largest publisher in the corpus.

## Proposed remediation

Re-run the consolidator with:

1. **Expanded organization enum** — add ABS, ASCE, ASME, AWS, NACE, IEC, HSE (defect #1), unblocking #2.
2. **Filename heuristics** — pre-filter personal correspondence (defect #3), structural fragments (#5), and base64 trailing tokens (#7) before classification.
3. **Unknown-bucket reclassification pass** — run after #1 lands; expected to drain the bulk of the 629-doc bucket.
4. **Cross-series ASTM router** — committee-prefix routing for A/B/C/D/E/F/G (defect #6); fix BSI bucket as a side-effect of stricter publisher matching (#4).
5. **OCR backfill** — run OCR over the ASTM corpus (defect #8); current <1% coverage blocks any retrieval-grounded wiki page that would cite ASTM body text.

## Acceptance

- `_catalog.json` `statistics.by_organization` includes the 7 missing publishers.
- Unknown bucket drops from 629 to <100.
- ISO bucket size reflects real ISO standards (~112), not ~308.
- BSI bucket purity >95%.
- ASTM OCR coverage >50%.

## Notes

- Defect surfaced by parallel-agent confirmation, not single-source reading. Memory ref: cross-agent ingest patterns make consolidator-level structural defects visible that single-pass review misses.
- This issue is filed against `workspace-hub` (the orchestrator/pipeline repo), not the spinout `llm-wiki` content repo, because the defect is in the upstream consolidator tooling that feeds the wiki — not in wiki content.
issues.display_title: O&G-Standards consolidator: 8 catalog-classification defects surfaced by parallel-agent ingest

issues.title: Routine: /repo-sync + /mnt/local-analysis cleanup audit (every 2 days)
issues.body:
## Tracking issue for the recurring `/repo-sync` routine

**Schedule:** every 2 days at 5am Chicago (10am UTC) — cron `0 10 */2 * *`
**Routine ID:** `trig_01L3z5Q99KrmTgfEa9jhQBNo`
**Manage:** https://claude.ai/code/routines/trig_01L3z5Q99KrmTgfEa9jhQBNo

The routine posts a status comment to this issue on every run. Each comment is a single markdown table:

| scope | action | count | notes |
|---|---|---|---|

Followed by a `## DECISION-PENDING` section listing anything that needs human judgment (dirty worktrees, push-blocked branches, mass-deletion fingerprints matching the wave-dump pattern, etc.).

## Operating context

The manual `/repo-sync` resume on 2026-05-01 cleaned 53 worktrees and freed ~36GB. Baseline going forward:
- `/mnt/local-analysis/` should be ~1 top-level dir (`workspace-hub`) plus optional siblings
- `workspace-hub` registered worktrees: ~5 (active only, no detached or orphaned)
- `acma-projects`: fully materialized (368K files, sparse disabled, 0 skip-worktree bits)

## Iron Law for routine runs

- NO `git push --force`, NO `git reset --hard`
- NO auto-resolve of merge conflicts
- NO `git commit --no-verify`
- `git push --no-verify` IS allowed for preservation-only branch pushes
- Anything ambiguous → `DECISION-PENDING`, never decide on the user's behalf

## Reacting to a routine comment

- Zero `DECISION-PENDING`: drift under control, nothing to do.
- Non-empty `DECISION-PENDING`: triage. Common patterns:
  - New `codex/*` branches with unique commits → `--no-verify` push or patch-export
  - Mass-deletion fingerprint (~31K dirty `D` rows) → sparse-disable artifact, restore via `git checkout HEAD -- .`
  - Detached worktrees with no upstream → ancestry probe vs `origin/main`, then keep or remove

## Closing the issue

Don't close — this is a persistent watcher. To pause, toggle `enabled: false` at https://claude.ai/code/routines/trig_01L3z5Q99KrmTgfEa9jhQBNo

issues.title: Convert ROGII task brief PPTX to PDF on ace-linux-2 (LibreOffice required)
issues.body:
## Context

Working on the [ROGII Wellbore Geology Prediction](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/rogii-wellbore-geology-prediction) Kaggle competition (sibling repo at `/mnt/local-analysis/kaggle-rogii-2026/` on ace-linux-1, deadline 2026-08-05).

The competition's task brief is shipped as a 27.5 MB PPTX with 14 slides and 19 diagrams (well-trajectory views, GR-correlation figures, map and 3D views). Text content has been extracted via \`python-pptx\` to \`docs/task-brief.md\` already, but the diagrams need a proper PDF render.

ace-linux-1 has no LibreOffice and we don't want to install it there. ace-linux-2 has LibreOffice already (per user direction 2026-05-05). Defer the conversion to that machine.

## Source

\`AI_wellbore_geology_prediction_task_en.pptx\` (27.5 MB), located at:
- ace-linux-1: \`/mnt/ace/kaggle-rogii-2026/data/raw/AI_wellbore_geology_prediction_task_en.pptx\`
- Reproducible via \`scripts/download_data.sh\` in the kaggle-rogii-2026 repo (uses Kaggle CLI; user must have OAuth via \`kaggle auth login\` set up on the destination machine).

## What to do on ace-linux-2

\`\`\`bash
# Once kaggle-rogii-2026 repo is accessible on ace-linux-2 (see Open Questions below):
cd kaggle-rogii-2026
./scripts/bootstrap_data_dir.sh   # idempotent symlink setup
./scripts/download_data.sh        # materializes ~1.3 GB dataset incl. the PPTX
soffice --headless --convert-to pdf --outdir docs \\
    data/raw/AI_wellbore_geology_prediction_task_en.pptx
mv docs/AI_wellbore_geology_prediction_task_en.pdf docs/task-brief.pdf
git add docs/task-brief.pdf && git commit -m \"docs: add PDF render of task brief\"
\`\`\`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] \`docs/task-brief.pdf\` exists in the kaggle-rogii-2026 repo.
- [ ] PDF contains all 14 slides with diagrams visible (visual spot-check on slides 9, 12–13 — those carry the modeling-relevant figures).
- [ ] PDF size sanity check: ≥ 5 MB (anything smaller suggests images were dropped during conversion).
- [ ] Commit lands and is pushed if the repo has a remote at that point.

## Open questions / dependencies

1. **Repo accessibility on ace-linux-2.** The kaggle-rogii-2026 sibling repo is currently local-only on ace-linux-1 (no GitHub remote). Two paths:
   - Push kaggle-rogii-2026 to a new GitHub repo (\`vamseeachanta/kaggle-rogii-2026\`, public or private). Cleanest but requires user decision on visibility/license.
   - Bundle the repo via \`git bundle\` and copy to ace-linux-2 manually.
2. **Kaggle CLI auth on ace-linux-2.** Will need a separate \`kaggle auth login\` OAuth flow on that machine, or copy of \`~/.kaggle/credentials.json\` (preferred to re-auth fresh).

## Why deferred (and not just sudo'd here)

User direction 2026-05-05: \"ace-linux-2 has libreoffice. Let us just keep this task for that machine. Add a new issue for it.\" Avoids ~400 MB of LibreOffice packages on ace-linux-1 where they wouldn't be reused.

issues.title: feat(solver-queue): hands-off multi-machine inbox ingestion for OrcaWave, OrcaFlex, and AQWA
issues.body:
## Summary
Add a hands-off multi-machine solver batch pipeline so a user can drop manifests/input files into a known inbox, have Linux hosts ingest/queue them, and have Windows licensed hosts run OrcaWave, OrcaFlex, and AQWA/ANSYS jobs via periodic polling without manually touching the machines.

## Current evidence
- Existing solver queue exists: `queue/pending/` -> `queue/completed/` or `queue/failed/`, documented in `docs/solver/README.md` and `queue/job-schema.yaml`.
- Existing submission path supports only `orcawave` and `orcaflex`: `scripts/solver/submit-job.sh`, `scripts/solver/submit-batch.sh`, `scripts/solver/validate_manifest.py`.
- `ace-linux-2` is reachable and has AI/dev/open-source simulation tooling, but does **not** have OrcaWave, OrcaFlex, AQWA/ANSYS, MATLAB, or Python `OrcFxAPI`; it should coordinate/ingest/preprocess, not execute licensed solver jobs.
- `ace-linux-2` NFS access to the ace-linux-1 knowledge/data center is via `/mnt/remote/ace-linux-1/ace`, not direct `/mnt/ace`.
- `ace-linux-2` cron is drifted and points at stale `/mnt/workspace-hub` paths while the observed workspace is `/mnt/local-analysis/workspace-hub`.
- `licensed-win-1` / `licensed-win-2` are registry-designated OrcaFlex/ANSYS hosts, but no SSH access is configured; Windows Task Scheduler/Git Bash is the current execution route.

## Required design
1. Define canonical inbox/drop locations and file contract:
   - repo inbox: `queue/inbox/` for Git-backed manifests
   - optional shared-store inbox under `/mnt/ace/...` on ace-linux-1 and `/mnt/remote/ace-linux-1/ace/...` on ace-linux-2
   - Windows-local workspace path mapping for `D:\workspace-hub`
2. Add a cron-safe ingestion wrapper that scans the inbox, validates manifests, atomically stages accepted jobs into `queue/pending/`, moves invalid submissions to quarantine, logs every action, and commits/pushes only accepted queue changes.
3. Extend schema/validation/submission for `aqwa` or `ansys-aqwa` jobs with explicit input/output patterns and batch command contract.
4. Extend Windows queue processor dispatch to route jobs by solver and host capability:
   - OrcaWave/OrcaFlex on licensed Orcina host
   - AQWA/ANSYS on ANSYS host
   - no licensed solver execution on ace-linux-2
5. Add scheduled-task definitions in `config/scheduled-tasks/schedule-tasks.yaml` and Windows Task Scheduler installation notes/scripts for licensed hosts.
6. Repair or supersede ace-linux-2 cron path drift using canonical schedule rendering.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A manifest/input dropped into the canonical inbox is ingested without manual machine access.
- [ ] Valid OrcaWave/OrcaFlex jobs appear in `queue/pending/` and are picked up by licensed Windows queue processing.
- [ ] AQWA/ANSYS jobs validate through schema and route to the ANSYS-capable host instead of being rejected as unknown solver types.
- [ ] Invalid submissions are quarantined with actionable error logs, not silently ignored.
- [ ] `ace-linux-2` scheduled tasks use `/mnt/local-analysis/workspace-hub` or a verified symlink/path contract, not stale `/mnt/workspace-hub` references.
- [ ] Tests cover manifest validation, inbox ingestion, atomic moves/quarantine, and solver dispatch selection.
- [ ] Documentation explains roles: ace-linux-1 control plane, ace-linux-2 ingestion/preprocess/overflow worker, licensed Windows hosts solver execution.

## Related
- Parent/related: #1586 solver queue hardening
- Related: #2170 Windows licensed tool probe adapters
- Related: #1564 ace-linux-2 crontab sync
- Related: #1119 multi-machine work distribution

issues.title: Post-update display/VNC recovery on ace-linux-2
issues.body:
## Context
After OS update on ace-linux-2, the KVM display (NVIDIA T400 + EDID drop) and VNC access likely need re-validation and re-application of the fix.

## Root Cause (WRK-307)
NVIDIA T400 loses EDID signal when KVM switches away. Wayland makes it worse. X11 + forced EDID config is the workaround. OS updates can reset:
- `/etc/gdm3/custom.conf` (re-enable Wayland)
- Kernel DRM card numbering (`card2-DP-3` may change)
- NVIDIA driver DFP-N mappings
- Stale EDID in `/etc/X11/edid.bin`

## Existing Scripts
- `scripts/operations/system/fix-kvm-display-ace-linux-2.sh`
- `scripts/operations/connection/vnc-ace-linux-2.sh`

## Steps
1. SSH verify: `ssh vamsee@ace-linux-2 'echo ok'`
2. Check Wayland state: `grep WaylandEnable /etc/gdm3/custom.conf`
3. Check NVIDIA driver: `nvidia-smi`
4. Check DRM card numbering: `ls /sys/class/drm/ | grep DP`
5. Re-run display fix: `bash scripts/operations/system/fix-kvm-display-ace-linux-2.sh`
6. If card numbering changed, update the fix script + re-capture EDID
7. Verify KVM display works after switching away and back
8. Verify VNC: `bash scripts/operations/connection/vnc-ace-linux-2.sh`
9. Permanent fix: DP EDID emulator dongle (~$10)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] KVM display works (switch away and back without loss)
- [ ] Wayland confirmed disabled in GDM
- [ ] EDID captured and Xorg config applied
- [ ] DRM card mapping verified and script updated if changed
- [ ] VNC connection works from dev-primary

- The exact literal path `/mnt/ace-data/raw data` does **not** exist.
- Metadata-only discovery found 14 raw-like directories under `/mnt/ace-data` (`raw`, `raw_data`, or `Raw`), with no raw content copied into git/wiki.
- Existing overlap must be preserved: vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#13 is the llm-wiki roadmap anchor, vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2392 is the coverage-gap detector issue, and vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2487 already delivered the raw-data-to-readiness spine/control-plane.

## Problem
The raw-like mounted source estate is not yet consistently classified into:
1. llm-wiki/document-intelligence candidates,
2. existing/in-flight coverage,
3. code/vendor/internal exclusions,
4. private/project-sensitive exclusions, and
5. future source-family package candidates requiring separate approval.

Without this metadata-only triage layer, agents risk either missing high-value source families or over-promoting raw/private/project data into git/wiki.

## Metadata-only inventory evidence
Representative discovered raw-like directories:

| Source path | Metadata-only count | Initial routing |
|---|---:|---|
| `/mnt/ace-data/O&G-Standards/raw` | 28,803 files / 692 dirs | standards candidate, reconcile with vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#25/#2373/#2392/#2487 and completed bounded standards promotions |
| `/mnt/ace-data/client_projects/energy_bsee/raw_data` | 10 files | offshore/BSEE candidate; no direct duplicate issue found |
| `/mnt/ace-data/digitalmodel/docs/aqwa/data/scripts/mooring_analysis/raw` | 28 files | AQWA candidate; map to vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2103 rather than duplicate |
| `/mnt/ace-data/digitalmodel/docs/orcaflex/literature/examples/raw` | 38 files / 76 dirs | OrcaFlex examples candidate; map to vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2124 rather than duplicate |
| `/mnt/ace-data/frontierdeepwater/data/raw` | 4 files / 1 dir | offshore source candidate; no direct duplicate issue found |
| `/mnt/ace-data/worldenergydata/data/modules/hse/raw` | 97 files / 7 dirs | HSE/safety data candidate; no direct duplicate issue found |
| `/mnt/ace-data/docs/disciplines/misc/projects/0136_das/.../Data/Raw` | 215 files / 8 dirs | indexed as `acma-projects`/project-management gap; project-sensitive until separately approved |

Non-corpus/exclusion examples include empty `.gitkeep` raw dirs, Rust crate internals, Struts image assets, QGIS generated DXF output, SSI marketing images, OPM parser source internals, and similar code/vendor/generated/personal/project-sensitive surfaces.

## Scope
Create a canonical plan for a metadata-only raw-like source triage and routing artifact. The plan should:
- preserve the raw-data boundary: no copying/promoting raw content to git/wiki;
- classify discovered raw-like roots by source family, sensitivity, target wiki/domain, existing issue mapping, and recommended next action;
- update or define a durable metadata/routing artifact under the document-intelligence surface;
- link resulting source-family work back to vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#13, vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2392, and vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2487;

## Out of scope

- No direct llm-wiki page generation from raw documents in this issue.
- No standards content extraction from proprietary/copyrighted documents.
- No project-sensitive corpus promotion (SESA/Woodfibre/ACMA/DAS/client material) without separate explicit approval.
- No implementation before canonical plan review and user approval.

issues.body:
## Summary

Three llm-wiki issues at `status:plan-approved` (#2368, vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2124, vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2125) have been stuck since 2026-04-28 due to a missing/stale approval-binding state. Codex's 10-thread parallel-implementation lanes correctly refused to execute, and the gate has held for 5+ days without remediation. This META issue captures the rot so it can be cleaned up in one pass.

## Why

Per the vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2460 contract (memory: `project_issue_2460_approval_binding.md`), `status:plan-approved` GitHub label is necessary but not sufficient — execution requires a revision-bound approval marker at `.planning/plan-approved/<n>.md` that names the approved plan SHA + review artifact paths. Otherwise agents can't confirm WHICH version of the plan was approved.

This was specifically designed as a load-bearing user-in-loop gate (memory: `feedback_never_offer_to_self_label_plan_approved.md`) — agents must NOT self-approve by creating the marker themselves.

The gate is doing its job. But the cleanup hasn't happened, and three valuable llm-wiki improvements have been frozen.

## Per-issue state (verified 2026-05-03)

### vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#22 faceted portal pages for large LLM-wiki domains

- GH labels: `status:plan-approved,status:working,agent:codex` ✓
- `.planning/plan-approved/2368.md`: **MISSING**
- Local plan `docs/plans/2026-04-23-issue-2368-faceted-portal-pages.md`: blob `b391641688` — header says `Status: draft` (REGRESSED from v2)
- Approved revision per Codex's 2026-04-28 comment: SHA `1c01062d8` — header in that SHA says `Status: draft (v2 — addresses r1 findings)`, blob `b1df634b3`
- Codex blocker comment: 2026-04-28T09:17:06Z (3 retry passes, all gated)
- Likely cause of plan regression: `feedback_merge_race_silent_revert.md` pattern during auto-sync

**Remediation:**
```bash
git checkout 1c01062d8 -- docs/plans/2026-04-23-issue-2368-faceted-portal-pages.md
# Then create .planning/plan-approved/2368.md with marker:
#   plan_sha: 1c01062d8

#   review_artifacts:
#     - scripts/review/results/2026-04-23-plan-2368-claude.md
#     - scripts/review/results/2026-04-23-plan-2368-codex.md
#     - scripts/review/results/2026-04-23-plan-2368-gemini.md
#   approved_by: vamseeachanta
#   approved_at: <ISO timestamp of human approval>
git add docs/plans/2026-04-23-issue-2368-faceted-portal-pages.md .planning/plan-approved/2368.md
git commit -m "markers(plan-approved): bind vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#22 to v2 SHA 1c01062d8"
```

### vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2124 extend ingestion to Orcina resources/examples/training

- GH labels: `status:plan-approved,status:working,agent:codex` ✓
- `.planning/plan-approved/2124.md`: **MISSING**
- Plan file: **MISSING** entirely (no `docs/plans/*2124*` exists)
- Codex blocker comment: 2026-04-28T09:18:13Z — also flags upstream dependency on vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2471 still being open
- Note: vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2471 status as of 2026-05-03 (verify before remediating)

**Remediation:** plan needs to be authored or located before binding. May be that the plan was lost to the same merge-race that ate vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#22's v2 content.

### vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2125 auto-refresh ingestion on Orcina releases

- GH labels: `status:plan-approved,status:working,agent:codex` ✓
- `.planning/plan-approved/2125.md`: **MISSING**
- Plan file: **MISSING** entirely (no `docs/plans/*2125*` exists)
- Codex 2026-04-28T06:15:27Z comment indicates an implementation pass DID complete: branch `codex/10thread-20260428-issue-2125`, commit `e4b6193236a70ed2ec960deb92b3f65b9f876616`. But no merge to main and label still says `status:working`.

**Remediation:** check if commit `e4b6193236` is salvageable; either land it or rebind plan + re-execute.

## Scope

This META issue is for **diagnosis + decision-making**, not implementation:

- Confirm the 3 issues' approval-binding state matches what's recorded above (re-verify before acting)

## Context

Issue [#117](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/117) acceptance criteria includes:
> Build shareable Jupyter notebook: production decline forecast (worldenergydata)

The `worldenergydata` library now has a production-ready `ArpsDeclineCurve` module at `worldenergydata.production.forecast.decline`. The GTM candidate review (2026-05-04) confirmed it works end-to-end:
- Hyperbolic, exponential, harmonic curve fitting via scipy
- EUR (Estimated Ultimate Recovery) calculation
- 240-month forecast with confidence intervals
- Plotly interactive visualization

A 63 KB FDAS GTM HTML report was already generated (`reports/gtm/2026-05-04-fdas-field-development-economics.html`), which includes an Arps decline demo with synthetic data.

## Scope

Create a standalone Jupyter notebook at `worldenergydata/notebooks/gtm_production_decline_forecast.ipynb`:

1. **Section 1: Module overview** — what Arps decline is, three model types, typical GoM/North Sea use cases
2. **Section 2: Synthetic demo** — fit a synthetic GoM well (qi=5000 bbl/month, Di=0.08/month, b=0.6), show EUR=146 Mbbls
3. **Section 3: Multi-well portfolio** — fit 3 hypothetical wells (early, mid, late decline stages), side-by-side comparison
4. **Section 4: Sensitivity** — how EUR changes with b (hyperbolic exponent) from 0.2 to 1.0
5. **Section 5: Connect to FDAS economics** — feed EUR directly into `EconomicsQuery.npv()` to compute field-level NPV from decline curve

All sections must run without external data (synthetic data generated in-notebook).

- [ ] Notebook executes end-to-end with `jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute` in <60 seconds

issues.body:
## Headline

Quality Gates' "20 failed, 3000 passed" report on digitalmodel main `60d59565` is the `pytest --maxfail=20` short-circuit ceiling, **NOT the true count**. A local repro on `60d59565` (without `--maxfail`) captured **184 unique FAILED + 60 unique ERROR = 244 broken tests** before the run was killed mid-collection. True count is likely higher — pytest never emitted its `=== short test summary ===` block.

The real number is **~12x larger** than CI reported.

## Evidence — bucket counts (local repro 2026-05-02 23:46Z)

### FAILED breakdown (184 unique)

| Bucket | Unique FAILED | Most-affected modules |
|---|---|---|
| `marine_ops/` | **77** | `legacy/test_mooring_catenary.py`, `test_mooring_catenary.py`, `test_cathodic_protection_dnv.py`, `legacy/test_component_database.py`, `test_unified_rao_reader.py`, `environmental_loading/test_ocimf.py`, `legacy/test_wave_spectra.py`, `test_catenary_adapter.py`, `integration/test_*` |
| `solvers/` | **33** | `orcaflex/test_orcaflex_cli.py` (26), `orcaflex/modular_generator/`, `orcaflex/mooring-tension-iteration/`, `orcaflex/reporting/test_*_fixture_snapshot.py` |
| `hydrodynamics/` | **25** | `diffraction/test_cli_integration.py` (12), `diffraction/test_benchmark_runner.py` (4), `diffraction/test_solver_smoke_unit.py`, `diffraction/test_unit_box_benchmark.py` |
| `infrastructure/` | **20** | `core/test_database_manager.py` (14), `core/test_cache.py` (4), `contracts/test_api_contracts.py` |
| `field_development/` | **16** | `test_economics.py` (TestCarbonSensitivity, TestFiscalRegimeTaxAdjustment, TestScheduleDeclineIntegration) |
| `orcaflex/` | **4** | `test_mooring_design.py` catenary, `test_installation_analysis.py` DAF |
| Other | **9** | naval_architecture (2), reservoir (2), orcawave (2), solver (2), contracts (2), simple_engine (1) |
| **Total FAILED** | **184** | |

### ERROR breakdown (60 unique — collection-time / fixture problems)

| Bucket | Unique ERROR | Most-affected modules |
|---|---|---|
| `infrastructure/` | **36** | `core/test_cache.py` (28 — Redis fixture missing), `core/test_database_manager.py` (8 — SQL fixture missing) |
| `solvers/` | **13** | `blender_automation/test_batch_processor.py` (4), `orcaflex/modular_generator/test_campaign_generator.py` (6), `orcaflex/test_orcaflex_converter_enhanced.py` (3) |
| `orcawave/` | **5** | `test_builder_orchestration.py` (4), `test_report_builder.py` (1) |
| `hydrodynamics/` | **3** | `passing_ship/test_passing_ship_cli.py` (2), `aqwa/test_aqwa_lis_parser_real_data.py` |
| `data_systems/` | **3** | `test_config_loader.py` validate_schema |
| **Total ERROR** | **60** | |

## Inferred root-cause clusters (need verification before per-bucket issue creation)

- **Marine ops mass-failure (77)** — concentration in `legacy/`, `catenary/`, `test_mooring_catenary.py` (12 tests), `test_cathodic_protection_dnv.py` (16 tests) suggests a SHARED dependency or fixture broke. Likely 1-3 root causes, not 77.
- **OrcaFlex CLI (26)** — all 26 in `test_orcaflex_cli.py` likely mean the CLI command isn't registered/findable on PATH in the local env. Single fix.
- **Infrastructure cache+db_manager (36 ERROR + 18 FAILED)** — Redis/SQL service deps absent locally. Verify against [#2585](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2585) inventory to ensure no overlap.
- **Field-dev economics (16)** — TestCarbonSensitivity, TestFiscalRegimeTaxAdjustment, TestScheduleDeclineIntegration — these look like REAL bugs in a feature [#2076](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2076) / [#2079](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2079) / [#2081](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2081) thought was working. - **Hydrodynamics diffraction (25 + 3 ERROR)** — `test_cli_integration.py` 12 failures all CLI-flavored — same CLI-not-on-PATH pattern as orcaflex CLI? Or different root cause? Needs investigation.

issues.title: epic(digitalmodel-ci): domain-divided CI architecture replacing maxfail-masking pattern
issues.body:
## Why now

This session surfaced that digitalmodel's QG suite has been chronically green-washed by \`maxfail=20\` masking 200+ pre-existing failures across 53 test files. The admin-merge-via-Quality-Gates-failure pattern (PRs [#541](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/541), [#544](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/544), [#549](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/549), [#550](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/550), [#551](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/551), [#553](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/553), [#568](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/568), [#569](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/569)) is now the default merge path — operationally fast but strategically corrosive: every PR carries the same 'gate trips on unrelated debt' justification.

Root cause: a single repo-wide \`pytest --maxfail=20\` invocation can't distinguish 'this PR introduced a regression in its own scope' from 'unrelated debt elsewhere in the repo.' Per-domain CI fixes both.

## Architecture

**14-15 test domains** (per [#2616](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2616) sweep + tests/ tree):

\`asset_integrity\`, \`citations\`, \`contracts\`, \`field_development\`, \`hydrodynamics-diffraction\`, \`hydrodynamics-passing-ship\`, \`infrastructure-core\`, \`marine-engineering\`, \`naval-architecture\`, \`orcaflex\`, \`orcaflex-solver\`, \`solver-smoke\`, \`specialized\`, \`structural\`, \`workflows\`, \`misc\`

Each domain becomes:
- a separate pytest job in a GH Actions matrix
- with its own \`--with\` dep list (so e.g. redis/psycopg2/motor only attach to \`infrastructure-core\`, not the whole CI)
- with its own conftest fixtures and skipif policies
- with the existing \`maxfail\` removed (per-domain failure counts stay bounded by domain size)

## Decisions locked (this session, vamseeachanta)

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Domain owner | All domains owned by \`vamseeachanta\` (single owner; CODEOWNERS encodes this) |
| Aggregator gate policy | **All domains must pass** for merge (no informational-only mode) |
| Run cadence | **Touched-domains-only on PRs**; **full matrix nightly** (cron) |
| Deprecation policy | No test deletion or blanket-skip without AI-attested 'source X is gone, no other consumers' commit per \`feedback_attestation_enables_contradiction_detection\` |

## Sub-tasks

- [ ] **A** — Domain inventory PR (\`tests/DOMAINS.md\` mapping every test directory → domain → dep set; informs all subsequent PRs). Read-only repo analysis. \`digitalmodel\`.
- [ ] **B** — \`.claude/quality-gates.yaml\` refactor: one gate per domain with its own command + deps. Aggregator gate depends on all. Drops repo-wide \`maxfail\`. \`digitalmodel\`.
- [ ] **C** — GH Actions matrix workflow: \`.github/workflows/quality-gates-by-domain.yml\` with \`strategy.matrix.domain\` for parallel runs + aggregator job. \`digitalmodel\`.
- [ ] **D** — Touched-domain detection: PR-time job that diffs changed paths against \`tests/DOMAINS.md\` and emits the matrix subset to run. Nightly cron uses full matrix. \`digitalmodel\`.
- [ ] **E** — Per-domain conftest extraction: move shared fixtures/skipifs from \`tests/conftest.py\` into each domain's local conftest. ~1 PR per domain (small each). \`digitalmodel\`.
- [ ] **F** — CODEOWNERS file with \`vamseeachanta\` as default owner. \`digitalmodel\`.
- [ ] **G** — Update workspace-hub agents.md + CLAUDE.md to encode the 'always test by domain during development' rule for AI agents. \`workspace-hub\`.

## After A-G land, the deferred cluster work re-routes by domain

| Cluster | Issue | New domain home |
|---|---|---|
| A — sys.modules pollution | [#2623](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2623) | \`contracts\` domain |

**Source:** #2552 plan-review queue audit 2026-05-03. Per [#2552 approval marker](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/blob/main/.planning/plan-approved/2552.md), the runbook content was approved despite a 4+ day Tier-D persistent-MAJOR pattern (claude/codex/gemini all MAJOR across 4+ rounds). The architectural defects under those MAJORs are deferred here for a focused fresh plan.

## Defects to address (from latest reviews)

### 1. Privacy-leaking test (Gemini, repeat)
The proposed `test_runbook_references_triggering_issues_without_personal_name` requires hardcoding the external commenter's PII into the test file to assert its absence. **Resolution:** drop the negative-presence assertion; only positively assert presence of issue numbers (#2401, #2546, #2550).

### 2. Undefined ingestion vector under `collaborators_only` lockdown (Gemini, repeat)
Plan tells operators to reply via `CONTRIBUTOR_INTEREST_TEMPLATE` but #2546's `collaborators_only` lockdown blocks the input channel. **Resolution:** explicitly define the ingestion vector (likely email or a designated public form) since GitHub interactions are blocked.

### 3. Security-posture contradiction in scenario 3 (Gemini, repeat)
Scenario 3 suggests "temporary lift of interaction limit" — globally undermines #2546's lockdown for one request. **Resolution:** either (a) drop scenario 3 entirely from in-scope work, or (b) define a per-user allowlist mechanism that doesn't lift the global limit.

### 4. Plan-internal contradictions (Claude, repeat)
- Untestable acceptance criteria (negative-presence checks for arbitrary unspecified strings)
- HTML-comment metadata contradicts surrounding table (plan was patched in layers without re-reading itself)

**Resolution:** restart from a clean T1 spec; do not iterate on the existing plan.

## Acceptance

- [ ] New plan filed under `docs/plans/` addressing items 1-4 explicitly
- [ ] Plan goes through one Claude+Gemini review cycle (Codex skipped per #2479 unless version-pin lands first)
- [ ] No regression on the runbook content already approved via #2552

## Severity

Medium — the runbook content is live (approved); this issue prevents drift between the runbook and its enforcement layer.

issues.title: policy(digitalmodel-tests): Cluster D — decide whether redis/psycopg2/motor belong in QG suite (51 errors)
issues.body:
## Context

Surfaced during [#2616](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2616). 51 errors in \`tests/infrastructure/core/\` are environmental — pure dep-wall, not feature defects.

## Affected

- \`tests/infrastructure/core/test_cache.py\` (32 errors) — requires \`redis\` backend
- \`tests/infrastructure/core/test_database_manager.py\` (19 errors) — logs \`No module named 'psycopg2'\` and references \`motor\` (async MongoDB)

These would also fail in the original CI run with the same env. Whether they were ever expected to run in the QG suite is a policy question.

## Decision needed

Pick one:

- **(a) Add deps to QG environment**: \`--with redis --with psycopg2-binary --with motor\` to the QG command. Keeps tests in the QG tier. Adds CI install time. Requires actual Redis/Postgres/Mongo containers in CI for tests to pass (not just import). Likely heaviest infrastructure lift.
- **(b) Mark with import-probe skipif**: add \`@pytest.mark.skipif(not _has_redis, reason=\"redis backend unavailable\")\` per-class in those test files. Cheap fix; tests skip cleanly when the backend isn't available; tests still run on machines that have Redis/Postgres/Mongo.
- **(c) Move to a separate \"integration\" tier outside QG**: e.g., a separate pytest mark or a dedicated tox env that QG doesn't invoke. Cleanest separation; requires a tier-routing decision.

Recommendation: (b) for fastest unblock; (c) for long-term cleanliness.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] 51 errors in \`tests/infrastructure/core/\` either pass (with backends installed) or skip cleanly (no errors)
- [ ] QG command produces 0 of these errors

- [#2129](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2129) — quality-gates audit umbrella

issues.title: fix(digitalmodel-tests): Cluster A — sys.modules pollution leaking MagicMock into tests/contracts/ (2 failures)
issues.body:
## Context

Surfaced during [#2616](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2616). Two tests in \`tests/contracts/\` fail in the full suite but pass in isolation — classic test-pollution Heisenbug, made deterministic by \`-p no:randomly\`.

## Defect

- \`tests/contracts/test_assetutilities_common_contract.py::test_update_deep_dictionary_importable\` → \`AssertionError: <MagicMock> == 1\`
- \`tests/contracts/test_assetutilities_data_contract.py::test_AttributeDict_importable\` → \`AssertionError: <MagicMock> == 'value'\`

## Root cause

Some upstream test in the suite registers \`assetutilities.common.update_deep\` and \`assetutilities.common.data\` (or similar \`assetutilities.*\` modules) as \`MagicMock()\` in \`sys.modules\` without restoring them. With \`-p no:randomly\` the ordering is deterministic, so the pollution is reproducible. When the contract tests later import the real symbols they receive the mock.

## Verification

\`pytest tests/contracts/\` in isolation → **17/17 pass**. Sibling repo \`../assetutilities/src/assetutilities/common/update_deep.py\` carries both \`update_deep_dictionary\` and \`AttributeDict\` correctly.

## Fix options

- **(a) Hunt the polluter** — search candidates: tests that \`import unittest.mock; sys.modules[...] = MagicMock()\` or \`@patch.dict('sys.modules', ...)\` without proper teardown. Similar to the existing \`tests/conftest.py:92\` pattern for \`digitalmodel.subsea.catenary_riser.legacy.catenary_riser_summary\`. Then add proper teardown to that test.
- **(b) Defensive autouse fixture** in \`tests/contracts/conftest.py\` that purges polluted entries before each test:
  \`\`\`python
  for k in list(sys.modules):
      if k.startswith('assetutilities') and isinstance(sys.modules[k], MagicMock):
          del sys.modules[k]
  \`\`\`

Recommend (a) for the right fix; (b) as a safety net if (a) requires more bisection time than is available.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both contract tests pass in the full suite under \`-p no:randomly\`
- [ ] If (a): polluter identified and fixed; \`tests/contracts/\` no longer needs special handling
- [ ] If (b): conftest fixture documented with the polluter's path so it can be revisited

## Related

- [#2616](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2616)

issues.title: feat(workstations): add reusable Hermes preflight readiness checker
issues.body:
## Summary

Build a reusable workstation preflight checker for Hermes-led cross-machine dispatch. The checker should turn the manual `ace-linux-2` probe from #2519/#2520 into a repeatable command that verifies host reachability, login-shell tool visibility, provider runtime readiness, GitHub auth state, repo cleanliness, and engineering-tool smoke readiness before work is assigned.

## Motivation

#2519 established that `ace-linux-2` can run Hermes/Codex only through a login shell and that `gh` auth can independently be invalid. This needs to become an automated gate so future workstations are not delegated work based on stale or partial assumptions.

## Scope

- Add a script/CLI entrypoint for workstation preflight checks.
- Support at least `ace-linux-1` local mode and `ace-linux-2` remote mode.
- Use login-shell checks for remote machines where user-level tools live under `~/.local/bin` or `~/.npm-global/bin`.
- Check and redact-sensitive-report:
  - hostname / reachability / canonical workspace path,
  - git repo branch/status/ahead-behind for tier-1 repos,
  - `gh auth status` and `gh api user` success/failure without token values,
  - Hermes provider/model config without secrets,
  - `codex`, `claude`, `gemini` command availability/version,
  - selected engineering tool presence/smoke checks.
- Emit both JSON and markdown reports under `docs/reports/` or a configured artifacts directory.
- Return non-zero only for clearly blocking failures; classify warnings vs blockers.

## Acceptance criteria

- A documented command can run the preflight against `ace-linux-2` via:
  `ssh ace-linux-2 'bash -lc "<probe>"'` or equivalent.
- Output never includes token/auth file contents.
- The current `ace-linux-2` `gh` auth failure is represented as a GitHub-mutation blocker, not as a total machine failure.
- Tests cover parsing/classification for at least reachable, auth-invalid, tool-missing, and clean-repo cases.
- The #2519 handoff/prompts can reference this checker instead of embedding ad hoc shell snippets.

## Related

- Parent: #2519
- Blocker/auth repair: #2520
- Committed baseline report: `docs/reports/2026-04-27-issue-2519-ace-linux-2-readiness-probe.md`

issues.title: Set up Telegram mobile access for Hermes AI control
issues.body:
## Summary
Set up Telegram-based mobile access to Hermes/AI so Vamsee can interact with the agent, approve/adjust plans, tweak task lists, and monitor/steer work while on the move.

## Current user state
- Vamsee has logged into Telegram on the mobile device using phone/name.
- Next user-side action is to create a Telegram bot via `@BotFather`; the bot token must be handled as a secret and must not be pasted into public issue comments or chat logs.

## Recommended architecture
Use a Telegram **bot** connected to the Hermes gateway on `ace-linux-1`, not a separate human Telegram account for the AI.

Rationale:
- Telegram bots are the normal integration surface for programmatic message handling.
- Bot token can be stored in `~/.hermes/.env` and loaded by the gateway service.
- Access can be restricted to Vamsee's user/chat ID.
- Hermes gateway already supports Telegram and can run as a persistent service.

## Scope

### Phase 1 — Private single-user Telegram bot
- Create bot using `@BotFather`.
- Securely store bot token in `~/.hermes/.env` or password manager.
- Configure Hermes gateway Telegram integration.
- Restrict access to Vamsee's Telegram user/chat ID.
- Start gateway as persistent service on `ace-linux-1`.
- Verify mobile command/response loop.

### Phase 2 — Mobile operating guardrails
- Keep approval mode `manual` or `smart`; do not use approval `off` for mobile operation.
- Enable only mobile-appropriate toolsets initially.
- Confirm secrets are never transmitted through Telegram.
- Document restart/stop/status commands.
- Create quick-reference command sheet for on-the-move tweaks.

### Phase 3 — Optional enhancements after stable
- Voice-message STT/TTS for hands-free operation.
- Dedicated group/topic if DMs become cluttered.
- Additional user allowlist if needed.

## Task list
- [ ] Create Telegram bot with `@BotFather` from Vamsee's phone.
- [ ] Capture bot username and token securely; do not paste token into GitHub or chat.
- [ ] Configure Hermes gateway Telegram platform with `hermes gateway setup` or config edit.
- [ ] Add Telegram token to `~/.hermes/.env` and verify service can read it.
- [ ] Configure allowed users/chats to Vamsee only for initial rollout.
- [ ] Enable appropriate toolsets for mobile use: memory, session_search, cronjob, send_message, file, terminal, browser/web only as needed.
- [ ] Install/start gateway persistently: `sudo $(which hermes) gateway install --system`, then start/status.
- [ ] If systemd cannot see env vars, add `EnvironmentFile=/home/vamsee/.hermes/.env` to the service and restart.
- [ ] Test `/help`, `/status`, a simple task tweak, and a safe approval-gated action from mobile.
- [ ] Write a concise mobile command sheet for status checks, plan approvals, task-list updates, pause/kill commands, and GitHub-link requests.
- [ ] Optional: configure/test STT/TTS with one short voice note.

## Acceptance criteria
- Telegram bot responds to Vamsee from mobile through Hermes gateway.
- Unauthorized users/chats are blocked or ignored.
- Gateway survives shell logout/reboot via systemd or documented equivalent.
- Bot token is stored only in secret/config surfaces, not committed or posted.
- Mobile workflow supports: ask status, tweak a task list, request a GitHub link, and approve/revise/hold a plan.
- Quick-reference command sheet exists in a durable repo/docs location.

## Security / operations notes
- Do not paste the bot token into this issue.
- Prefer single-user allowlist for the first rollout.
- Keep mobile destructive actions approval-gated.
- Avoid approval mode `off` unless explicitly approved for a bounded test.

issues.body:
## Context

Commit [`2c185d2d`](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/commit/2c185d2d) (2026-03-24, "fresh repo after slimming") added 26 entries to `digitalmodel/tests/conftest.py:collect_ignore` without filing follow-up issues. A subsequent commit `4515cd01` (2026-05-01, via [#2574](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2574)) added 3 more entries — those 3 ARE tracked in [#2580](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2580). The other 26 are documented-but-unowned: comments say *why* they're skipped, but no owner, no exit criteria, no link to a fix plan.

Audit reference: [`docs/sessions/2026-05-02-collect-ignore-cumulative-audit.md`](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/blob/main/docs/sessions/2026-05-02-collect-ignore-cumulative-audit.md)

This umbrella issue exists so that closing [#2580](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2580) does not silently leave 90% of the `collect_ignore` list untracked.

## Inventory (26 untracked entries)

All paths relative to `digitalmodel/tests/`. Line numbers refer to `digitalmodel/tests/conftest.py` at HEAD as of 2026-05-02.

| # | Path | Bucket | Inline comment | Line |
|---|------|--------|----------------|------|
| 1 | `marine_ops/artificial_lift/dynacard/test_vision_benchmark.py` | A. Missing local modules | "standalone scripts, not real tests" | 11 |
| 2 | `solvers/orcaflex/examples_integration/test_converter.py` | A. Missing local modules | same | 12 |
| 3 | `solvers/orcaflex/examples_integration/test_single_download.py` | A. Missing local modules | same | 13 |
| 4 | `structural/fatigue_analysis/test_reference_seastate_scaling.py` | A. Missing local modules | same | 14 |
| 5 | `visualization/design_tools/pilot_program/test_case_1_separator.py` | A. Missing local modules | same | 15 |
| 6 | `solvers/orcaflex/test_orcaflex_unit.py` | B. Missing src modules | "not yet implemented" | 17 |
| 7 | `structural/fatigue_apps/test_load_scaling.py` | B. Missing src modules | same | 18 |
| 8 | `subsea/pipeline/test_on_bottom_stability.py` | B. Missing src modules | same | 19 |
| 9 | `test_plate_capacity.py` | B. Missing src modules | same | 20 |
| 10 | `visualization/test_anomaly_detection.py` | C. Deleted orcaflex-dashboard | "Deleted orcaflex-dashboard service files" | 22 |
| 11 | `visualization/test_comparative_analysis.py` | C. Deleted orcaflex-dashboard | same | 23 |
| 12 | `visualization/test_component_classifier.py` | C. Deleted orcaflex-dashboard | same | 24 |
| 13 | `visualization/test_csv_parser.py` | C. Deleted orcaflex-dashboard | same | 25 |
| 14 | `visualization/test_data_validator.py` | C. Deleted orcaflex-dashboard | same | 26 |
| 15 | `visualization/test_loading_decoder.py` | C. Deleted orcaflex-dashboard | same | 27 |
| 16 | `visualization/test_sensitivity_analysis.py` | C. Deleted orcaflex-dashboard | same | 28 |
| 17 | `visualization/test_statistical_analysis.py` | C. Deleted orcaflex-dashboard | same | 29 |
| 18 | `workflows/orcawave/test_com_connection.py` | D. Platform-specific / optional deps | "Platform-specific or missing optional deps" | 31 |
| 19 | `workflows/orcawave/test_end_to_end.py` | D. Platform-specific / optional deps | same | 32 |
| 20 | `workflows/orcawave/test_integration.py` | D. Platform-specific / optional deps | same | 33 |
| 21 | `workflows/standalone/markitdown/test_converter.py` | D. Platform-specific / optional deps | same | 34 |
| 22 | `test_workflow_checkpoints.py` | E. pytest-asyncio / hypothesis conflict | "Requires pytest-asyncio plugin (disabled due to hypothesis conflict)" | 36 |
| 23 | `marine_ops/marine_engineering/test_component_database.py` | F. Data file deps not in git | "hull profiles and chain database" | 38 |
| 24 | `hydrodynamics/hull_library/test_hull_library_expansion.py` | F. Data file deps not in git | same | 39 |
| 25 | `specialized/cathodic_protection/test_abs_ship_variants_wrk271.py` | G. CP random-ordering shared state | "fail intermittently with random ordering (shared state issue)" | 41 |
| 26 | `specialized/cathodic_protection/test_cathodic_protection_b401.py` | G. CP random-ordering shared state | same | 42 |

## Per-bucket triage suggestion

| Bucket | Entries | Suggested disposition |
|--------|---------|------------------------|
| A. Missing local modules | 1–5 | **Decide: convert to real tests OR delete.** Comment says "standalone scripts, not real tests" — if true, delete the files; if shippable as tests, port the missing local-module imports. Either way the `collect_ignore` line goes away. |
| B. Missing src modules | 6–9 | **Fix or delete.** "Not yet implemented" — pair each test with its missing src module, and either implement the module or delete the test. No permanent skips. |
| C. Deleted orcaflex-dashboard | 10–17 | **Delete the test files.** The service was deleted; the tests should follow. `collect_ignore` is the wrong durable home for "tests of deleted code". |
| D. Platform-specific / optional deps | 18–21 | **Convert to `pytest.importorskip` / `pytest.mark.skipif`.** Skip-at-collect via `collect_ignore` masks the *reason* on Linux CI; in-test markers express the dep gate cleanly and let Windows/with-deps runs exercise the code. |
| E. pytest-asyncio / hypothesis conflict | 22 | **Resolve the plugin conflict.** Either pin compatible versions or split the test from the hypothesis-using suite. Permanent skip is not acceptable for an async-checkpoint test. |
| F. Data file deps not in git | 23–24 | **Add fixtures or `pytest.skip` with `xfail`-style data-missing diagnostic.** Hull profiles and chain database belong in `tests/fixtures/` (small samples) or downloaded by a fixture builder; either way the test should run when data is present and skip with a clear pointer when not. |
| G. CP random-ordering shared state | 25–26 | **Fix the shared state.** This is a flake, not a skip-worthy condition — the tests should be deterministic regardless of ordering. Diagnose via `pytest -p no:randomly` to confirm, then isolate the shared state. |

## Acceptance criteria

This umbrella is satisfied when **every one of the 26 entries** has reached one of:

1. A dedicated sub-issue is filed and linked here, with a plan, and the entry is annotated in `conftest.py` with the issue number; OR
2. A real fix has landed that allows removal of the `collect_ignore` line (verified by removing the line and the test passing in CI); OR
3. A documented "permanent skip" justification exists at a stable doc path (e.g. `docs/decisions/`) AND the `conftest.py` comment cites that doc by path. The justification must explain why the test cannot be made to run on supported CI.

The umbrella issue itself does not deliver fixes — it tracks the disposition of every line. A close-out comment must enumerate the 26 entries and link each to its disposition (sub-issue, fix PR, or decision doc).

## Relationship to other issues

- **Sister to [#2580](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2580)** — that issue covers exactly 3 of the 29 `collect_ignore` entries (`citations/test_registry.py`, `citations/test_schema.py`, `asset_integrity/test_yml_utilities_additional.py`, lines 45/46/50 in `conftest.py`). Closing [#2580](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2580) alone leaves the 26 entries above untracked — this umbrella prevents that.
- **Cross-reference [#2414](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2414)** — title "test(ecosystem-sync): autobuild or skip missing local git fixtures" superficially looks similar to bucket F (data file deps), but the body confirms it scopes to `tests/ecosystem-sync/fixtures/repos/` in the **workspace-hub root**, not `digitalmodel/tests/`. **[#2414](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2414) does NOT cover any of the 26 entries above.** It remains its own concern.

## Labels — fallbacks used

The requested labels `tracker`, `area:testing`, and `repo:digitalmodel` do not exist on this repo (verified via `gh label list` 2026-05-02). Applied fallback:
- `domain:testing` (closest existing equivalent of `area:testing`)
- No equivalent of `tracker` or `repo:digitalmodel` exists; the title prefix `tracker(digitalmodel-tests):` carries that semantics in lieu of a label.
- No `status:needs-plan` label exists; left status unset (per project policy this issue lands at `status:plan-review` only after its own plan is drafted).

issues.body:
## Context
Claude, Codex, and Gemini agent configs are managed via repo templates in `config/agents/{claude,codex,gemini}/` and synced to home directories by `scripts/_core/sync-agent-configs.sh`. Hermes is not yet covered.

The `harness-update.sh` cron script already has `update_hermes()` but only runs on ace-linux-1. ace-linux-2 needs inclusion.

## What Needs to Happen

### A) Add Hermes templates to repo
- `config/agents/hermes/config.yaml.template` — model defaults, toolsets, terminal (no secrets)
- `config/agents/hermes/SOUL.md` — persona template

### B) Extend sync-agent-configs.sh
Add Hermes to `scripts/_core/sync-agent-configs.sh`:
- Template: `config/agents/hermes/config.yaml.template`
- Target: `~/.hermes/config.yaml`
- Merge strategy: template provides defaults, machine-local overrides preserved
- Skip auth.json and .env (secrets, never in repo)

### C) Custom skills versioning
- Bundled skills managed by `hermes update` (no action needed)
- Custom workflow skills → `config/agents/hermes/custom-skills/` in repo
- Sync script copies/symlinks to `~/.hermes/skills/`

### D) Add ace-linux-2 to harness-update cron
In `config/scheduled-tasks/schedule-tasks.yaml`:
```yaml
# Change from:
machines: [dev-primary, ace-linux-1]
# To:
machines: [dev-primary, ace-linux-1, dev-secondary, ace-linux-2]
```
Then run `setup-cron.sh` on ace-linux-2.

### E) Memories policy
- `MEMORY.md` and `USER.md` are personal/accumulated — do NOT sync via repo
- They build naturally per machine as Hermes is used
- Existing `claude-memory-backup` cron already backs up to ace-linux-2

- [ ] `config/agents/hermes/config.yaml.template` (new)
- [ ] `config/agents/hermes/SOUL.md` (new)
- [ ] `scripts/_core/sync-agent-configs.sh` (extend)

- [ ] `docs/ops/scheduled-tasks.md` (update documentation)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Hermes config template exists in repo
- [ ] sync-agent-configs.sh handles Hermes merge
- [ ] harness-update cron runs on ace-linux-2
- [ ] `bash scripts/_core/sync-agent-configs.sh --dry-run` shows Hermes sync
- [ ] Running sync on a new machine bootstraps Hermes config correctly

issues.title: data(field-dev): primary-source GoM equipment/cost source pack for #2112/#2055
issues.body:
## Summary
Create the next #2112 source-quality pass: a primary/public-source evidence pack for #2055's GoM field-development cost benchmarking gate.

This is a follow-up to the provisional artifact committed in `624c87f12`, which intentionally kept #2055 blocked because the candidate dataset failed source/semantic review.

## Parent / related
- Parent blocker: #2112
- Downstream benchmark feature: #2055
- Related field-development roadmap: #1842, #1861
- Current provisional report: `docs/reports/field-development-unblock-2112.md`
- Current provisional dataset: `data/field-development/gom-field-development-unblock-2112.json`

## Problem
The provisional dataset is useful as a source-lead list but is not correlation-ready. The adversarial review found that:

- `num_manifolds` was sometimes proxy-coded from drill centers/risers/field centers.
- `tieback_distance_km` mixed incompatible definitions.
- `cost_usd_bn` mixed public project costs with estimates/seed values.
- Some facts came from snippets or weak secondary references.

## Scope
Build a citable source pack and normalize definitions before any correlation/model implementation.

Required source-backed fields per accepted record:

| Field | Required interpretation |
|---|---|
| `num_trees` | actual subsea/wet tree count, or clearly sourced well/tree count |
| `num_manifolds` | actual subsea manifold/PLEM/PLET count only; no drill-center proxy |
| `tieback_distance_km` | one explicitly named definition, preferably subsea field/well/cluster to host/receiving facility |
| `cost_usd_bn` | project/phase cost with year/currency/scope; no generic cost-class seed |
| `source_notes` | durable public URL(s), source type, quote/paraphrase, confidence |

## Deliverables
- A source evidence table/report under `docs/reports/` or `.planning/intel/`.
- Updated dataset or companion JSON that distinguishes accepted records from rejected/needs-source records.
- A validator that fails if accepted records lack source/definition evidence.
- Clear recommendation on whether #2112 can close and whether #2055 can drop `status:needs-data`.

## Acceptance criteria
- At least 10 GoM records pass the public-source/no-invented-values semantic gate, **or** the report explicitly says fewer than 10 pass and keeps #2055 blocked.
- Every accepted numeric field has a durable public citation and consistent definition.
- No snippet-only, proxy-coded, or seeded numeric values are treated as accepted facts.
- #2055 remains `status:needs-data` unless the validator confirms the threshold.

## Execution constraints
- Plan first per repo policy; do not execute until approved.
- Use TDD/validator-first for the accepted-record gate.
- Prefer null + `needs_source` over estimates.
- Do not implement cost correlations until the source pack passes.

issues.body:
## Summary

Build cost-per-equipment-unit benchmark curves (cost/tree, cost/km-flowline, cost/manifold) by water-depth band, correlating SubseaIQ equipment counts against sanctioned project costs.

## Problem

The scaffold (#1861) provides `SubseaProject` with equipment-count fields and `load_projects()`, but zero cost functions exist. No module currently correlates equipment counts with project costs.

## Data Prerequisites (must be met before implementation)

- [ ] Equipment counts (num_trees, num_manifolds, tieback_distance_km) backfilled for >= 10 GoM fields in `data/field-development/subseaiq-scan-latest.json`
- [ ] Confirmed name-match mapping between SubseaIQ project names and CostDataPoint project names for overlapping records

## v1 Scope (band-level aggregation)

Use depth-band-level aggregation to compute cost-per-equipment ratios. This avoids per-project name-match fragility and works with sparse data.

### New functions in `digitalmodel/src/digitalmodel/field_development/benchmarks.py`:
- `cost_per_tree(projects) -> dict[str, float]` by depth band
- `cost_per_km_flowline(projects) -> dict[str, float]` by depth band
- `cost_per_manifold(projects) -> dict[str, float]` by depth band
- `unit_cost_curves(projects) -> dict` combining all three metrics
- `cost_benchmark_bands(projects) -> dict` with low/base/high by depth band and concept type

### New helper in `worldenergydata/subseaiq/analytics/cost_correlation.py`:
- `correlate_equipment_costs(subseaiq_records, cost_records)` — depth-band-level join
- `aggregate_costs_by_depth_band(merged)` — band-level cost aggregation

## Deferred to v2

- Per-project cost-per-tree correlation (requires CostDataPoint schema extension with equipment fields)
- Cross-validation of equipment-derived costs against individual sanctioned project costs
- Full 71-record equipment-count backfill

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Equipment counts populated for >= 10 GoM fields
- [ ] `cost_per_tree` returns values in $10M-$200M range per depth band
- [ ] `cost_per_km_flowline` returns values in $5M-$50M range per depth band
- [ ] `cost_per_manifold` returns physically reasonable values per depth band
- [ ] `cost_benchmark_bands` returns nested dict with low/base/high structure
- [ ] All 27 existing `test_benchmarks.py` tests pass unchanged
- [ ] New cost-related tests added and passing
- [ ] `benchmarks` exported from `digitalmodel.field_development.__init__`

## Dependencies

- #1861 (scaffold) — DONE
- Equipment-count data backfill — REQUIRED before implementation

## Labels

`enhancement`, `priority:high`, `cat:engineering`, `dark-intelligence`, `agent:claude`
