issues.title: [WRK] GTM: Vessel Installation Contractor Email Outreach Campaign
issues.body:
## Objective

Prepare and execute a go-to-market (GTM) email outreach campaign targeting **vessel installation contractors** as the first client segment for ACE Engineer consulting and AI-powered engineering services.

## Context

- ACE Engineer (Vamsee Achanta) offers deep subsea/offshore engineering expertise — hydrodynamics, mooring/riser design, structural analysis, OrcaFlex/OrcaWave, fatigue assessment
- An engineering chatbot pitch exists at `docs/strategy/engineering-chatbot-oilgas-pitch.md` with a phased capability roadmap (Knowledge Base → Document Intelligence → Analysis Pre-Processor → Review Assistant → Digital Advisor)
- Target segment: vessel installation contractors (EPIC contractors, pipelay/heavy-lift vessel operators, subsea installation companies)
- Goal: generate warm leads for engineering consulting engagements and/or AI-assisted engineering tool pilots

## Target Companies (Vessel Installation Contractors)

Research and compile a contact list of key companies including but not limited to:

1. **Tier 1 — Major EPIC / Installation Contractors**
   - Subsea7, TechnipFMC, Saipem, McDermott, Allseas, Heerema
   - Boskalis (Boskalis Subsea Services)
   - Van Oord (offshore wind installation)
   - DEME Offshore

2. **Tier 2 — Specialist Installation Vessel Operators**
   - DOF Subsea, Solstad Offshore, Bourbon Offshore
   - Sapura Energy, EMAS (now Ezra Holdings)
   - Seaway7 (Subsea7 renewables arm)
   - Coastline Maritime (cable/pipe installation)

3. **Tier 3 — Regional / Niche Players**
   - Cal Dive (now Helix Energy Solutions), Superior Energy Services
   - Global Industries legacy contacts
   - Gulf Offshore, DeepOcean Group

## Deliverables

### Phase 1 — Strategy & Templates (this issue)
- [ ] Define value proposition per company tier
- [ ] Draft 3 email templates (cold intro, follow-up, meeting request)
- [ ] Create a prospect contact list with company, contact name, title, email (research-based)
- [ ] Define email sequence timing (Day 0, Day 3, Day 7)
- [ ] Prepare a 1-page capability summary / attachment (PDF or link)

### Phase 2 — Personalization & Execution
- [ ] Personalize emails per company (reference their fleet, recent projects, pain points)
- [ ] Set up email tracking (open/click if tooling available)
- [ ] Execute first batch of outreach
- [ ] Log responses and schedule follow-ups

### Phase 3 — Measure & Iterate
- [ ] Track response rates by tier
- [ ] Refine messaging based on feedback
- [ ] Expand to adjacent segments (drilling contractors, FPSO operators, floating wind developers)

## Value Proposition Angles

| Angle | Message |
|-------|---------|
| **Engineering Efficiency** | Reduce analysis turnaround by 40-60% with AI-assisted OrcaFlex/structural workflows |
| **Knowledge Continuity** | Stop losing institutional knowledge when engineers leave — encode it in AI |
| **QC Multiplier** | AI-powered review catches errors that fatigued reviewers miss |
| **Junior Engineer Ramp-up** | New hires become productive 3x faster with an AI engineering mentor |
| **Cost Arbitrage** | Senior-level engineering insight at a fraction of full-time consultant rates |

## Email Template Structure

### Email 1 — Cold Introduction
- Subject line: problem-aware, specific to their operations
- Open with a relevant industry pain point (e.g., engineer shortage, project delays, rising analysis costs)
- Brief intro of capability (1-2 sentences)
- Specific offer (free 30-min consultation or a sample analysis)
- Clear CTA

### Email 2 — Follow-up (Day 3)
- Reference Email 1
- Share a concrete example / case study
- Lower-friction CTA (reply with availability)

### Email 3 — Meeting Request (Day 7)
- Final touch — direct calendar link
- Mention will reach out via LinkedIn if no response

## Files to Create

- `docs/strategy/gtm/vessel-installation-contractors/README.md` — campaign overview
- `docs/strategy/gtm/vessel-installation-contractors/prospect-list.md` — target companies and contacts
- `docs/strategy/gtm/vessel-installation-contractors/email-templates.md` — 3 email templates
- `docs/strategy/gtm/vessel-installation-contractors/value-proposition.md` — per-tier messaging
- `docs/strategy/gtm/vessel-installation-contractors/capability-summary.md` — 1-pager for attachment

## References

- `docs/strategy/engineering-chatbot-oilgas-pitch.md` — existing AI chatbot pitch
- `docs/BUSINESS_BRAIN.md` — ecosystem context
- `client_projects/energy_engineering/ecs/ecs_clients.md` — existing client contacts

## Success Criteria

- 20+ personalized emails sent to decision-makers at vessel installation contractors
- 3+ positive responses or meeting requests within 2 weeks
- At least 1 pilot engagement initiated within 30 days

issues.title: ace2: generate lifetime property imagery timelapse for 11511 Piping Rock
issues.body:
## Summary
Prepare the tooling and execution workflow on **ace-linux-2** to generate a property/neighborhood historical imagery timelapse GIF/MP4 for:

- Address: `11511 Piping Rock Dr., Houston, TX 77077`
- Approx geocode from Nominatim: `29.7397219, -95.5971637`
- Requested output: lifetime / longest practical visual progression showing how the property and neighborhood changed over time.

This is a machine-placement issue: keep **ace-linux-1** free as control plane and perform GIS/image-processing installation and heavy data work on **ace-linux-2**.

Related umbrella: #18

## Scope

### Phase 1 — ace-linux-2 setup/readiness
- Verify canonical workspace root: `/mnt/local-analysis/workspace-hub`.
- Use ace-linux-2 for dependency installation, imagery download/cache, frame rendering, and GIF/MP4 creation.
- Keep GitHub mutation authority on ace-linux-1 unless ace-linux-2 `gh auth` is repaired.
- Prefer a local project venv or uv-managed environment under ace-linux-2, not global Python pollution.
- Install/check likely dependencies: `earthengine-api`, `geemap`, `rasterio`, `imageio`, `pillow`, `geopandas`, `shapely`, `contextily`/`folium` as needed.
- Check GIS CLI availability already present on ace-linux-2: GDAL/QGIS are expected to be useful.

### Phase 2 — data-source strategy
Evaluate and document the best available imagery stack:
- Google Earth Pro historical imagery: best property-level visual source, but manual/API-limited.
- NAIP aerial imagery: best automatable open-data property/neighborhood source, roughly 2003-present where available.
- Landsat: 1984-present, useful for long-horizon neighborhood/urbanization, not parcel-scale.
- Sentinel-2: 2015-present, better recent medium-resolution context.

### Phase 3 — artifact generation
Generate at least one reviewable artifact:
- Property-scale GIF/MP4 around the address, preferred radius ~0.15–0.25 miles.
- Neighborhood-scale GIF/MP4, preferred radius ~1–2 miles.
- Year/date labels on frames.
- Static contact sheet or HTML report summarizing data sources, frame dates, limitations, and interpretation.

## Initial ace-linux-2 readiness evidence from ace-linux-1 probe

Probe timestamp: 2026-04-28 session.

- Host reachable: `ace-linux-2`.
- OS: Ubuntu Linux, kernel `6.17.0-22-generic`.
- Workspace root exists: `/mnt/local-analysis/workspace-hub`.
- Login-shell tools found on ace-linux-2:
  - `hermes`: `/home/vamsee/.local/bin/hermes`
  - `gh`: `/usr/bin/gh`
  - `gdalinfo`: `/usr/bin/gdalinfo`
  - `qgis`: `/usr/bin/qgis`
  - `python3`: `/usr/bin/python3`
  - `uv`: `/snap/bin/uv`
- ace-linux-2 `gh auth status`: token invalid; do not rely on ace-linux-2 for GitHub issue comments, PR creation, or pushes until repaired.

## Proposed execution notes

- ace-linux-1 should remain the GitHub/control-plane machine.
- ace-linux-2 can run a remote tmux worker via login shell, with logs under a durable location such as:
  - `/mnt/local-analysis/ace2-worker-logs/`
  - `/mnt/local-analysis/ace2-worker-reports/`
- Worker should write results and a short report locally, then ace-linux-1 can reconcile/post evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ace-linux-2 dependency environment created without disturbing ace-linux-1.
- [ ] Data-source feasibility matrix completed for this address.
- [ ] At least one generated GIF or MP4 exists for the property/neighborhood timeline.
- [ ] Static report/contact sheet documents imagery dates, radius, source, limitations, and recommended next step.
- [ ] If Google Earth Pro manual capture is required for true lifetime/high-res imagery, document the manual frame-capture workflow and fallback open-data workflow.
- [ ] All heavy install/data/cache work is performed on ace-linux-2.
- [ ] ace-linux-1 only handles issue/control-plane reconciliation.

## Guardrails

- Do not hardcode API keys or credentials.
- Do not perform GitHub mutation from ace-linux-2 until `gh auth` is valid there.
- Do not claim parcel-scale history from Landsat/Sentinel; use them for neighborhood context only.
- Keep artifacts shareable and clearly labeled with source/date/uncertainty.

issues.title: digitalmodel: CadQuery spike for parametric offshore geometry generation
issues.body:
## Context

CadQuery is a Python library for parametric 3D CAD on the OpenCASCADE B-rep kernel. STEP export is high-fidelity, so downstream meshers (gmsh, Salome) can control density without being trapped by authoring-time facets — a good shape for offshore component geometry that feeds AQWA.

Discovered via HN discussion 2026-04-17 (180 points, 47 comments): https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47772725

> **Revised 2026-04-17 per [adversarial review](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2327#issuecomment-4269065194)**: time-boxed; scope narrowed to one family and one pipeline; go/no-go criteria quantified; LLM-codegen question dropped (covered by #2328); current-state baseline required in plan.

## Scope

**Time-box:** 4 hours of hands-on work. Stop and report at the cap regardless of completeness.

**Target pipeline (committed):** STEP (CadQuery) → gmsh → AQWA `QPPL DIFF` panel diffraction. Chosen because panel diffraction has the tightest mesh-quality requirements (hardest pipeline test); digitalmodel already consumes AQWA downstream; OrcaFlex line-element path is a trivial follow-up if this works.

**Target family (committed):** H-link mooring shackle, 4 variants (MBL 45 t, 65 t, 85 t, 125 t). Chosen because mooring hardware is a recurring workspace-hub domain (#2070 cost-tracking, mooring-failures knowledge seed) and 4 variants exercises the "generate N from parameters" claim without inflating scope.

## Current State (document in the plan's Resource Intel section)

- Current `digitalmodel/` geometry pipeline — tools, inputs, outputs
- Where STEP files come from today (if at all)
- Which solver consumers exist and their geometry-input formats

## Go / No-Go Acceptance Criteria

All three must hold for **go**:

1. **Time-to-first-STEP < 30 min** for a Python-comfortable engineer working from CadQuery docs alone (no pre-existing exemplars)
2. **Regenerating all 4 H-link variants < 60 s** of compute total
3. **STEP → gmsh → AQWA `QPPL DIFF`** runs with no fatal mesh errors on first attempt for at least **2 of 4** variants

## Deliverable

- `digitalmodel/examples/cadquery-spike/h-link-family/` — 1 parametric script, 4 STEP outputs, 4 meshes, 1 successful AQWA run log
- `digitalmodel/examples/cadquery-spike/README.md` — timings, mesh quality notes, explicit verdict against the 3 criteria above

## Planning Workflow (per CLAUDE.md)

Plan file: `docs/plans/2026-MM-DD-issue-2327-cadquery-digitalmodel-spike.md` using `docs/plans/_template-issue-plan.md`. Resource-intel section must include the current-state documentation above. No implementation until `status:plan-approved`.

## References

- Wiki entity: `knowledge/wikis/engineering/wiki/entities/cadquery.md`
- Source summary: `knowledge/wikis/engineering/wiki/sources/2026-04-17-hn-cadquery.md`
- Marine cross-page: `knowledge/wikis/marine-engineering/wiki/entities/cadquery.md`
- Sibling issues: #2328 (tool comparison — covers the LLM-codegen question), #2329 (methodology decision — blocked by this)

issues.title: epic: zero-loss agent learnings — git-track ALL AI agent memories, corrections, patterns, and insights
issues.body:
## Context

A full audit of all 4 AI agents (Claude Code, Hermes, Codex, Gemini) revealed that **~6.7GB of machine-local state** has NO git protection. If ace-linux-1 dies, the entire institutional memory built over months of agent interaction is lost.

The learnings that matter most — user corrections, learned patterns, permission rules, cross-agent insights — total only ~400KB but are scattered across 4 different home directories with no unified backup or portability strategy.

This is the umbrella issue coordinating the fix across all agents.

## Architecture: Three Tiers of Portability

### Tier 1: Git-committed snapshots (survives `git clone`)
Small, high-value files snapshotted nightly into workspace-hub repo:
- Agent memory files (Hermes MEMORY.md/USER.md, Claude project memory, Codex rules)
- Distilled learning artifacts (patterns, corrections, insights, drift summaries)
- Exported session metadata (JSONL tool-call summaries, not full transcripts)

### Tier 2: Rsync backup (survives single-machine failure)
Large files backed up to ace-linux-2 daily:
- Full session transcripts (Claude 2.5GB, Codex 899MB, Gemini 162MB, Hermes 124MB)
- SQLite databases (Hermes state.db 53MB, Codex state_5.sqlite 59MB)

### Tier 3: Regenerable (no backup needed)
Caches, plugins, debug logs, telemetry — recreated on agent install.

## Child Issues

| # | Issue | Agent | What's tracked | Size | Status |
|---|-------|-------|---------------|------|--------|
| #1777 | Hermes memory snapshots | Hermes | MEMORY.md, USER.md | 3KB | NEW |
| #1778 | Un-gitignore hermes/cross-agent state | Hermes/Cross | hermes-insights.yaml, cross-agent-memory.yaml, session JSONL | 15KB+11MB | NEW |
| #1779 | Claude project memory snapshots | Claude | 39 feedback/project/reference memory files | 196KB | NEW |
| #1780 | Fix nightly pipeline git-add gap | Claude/All | corrections/, patterns/, cc-insights/, reflect-history/, learned-patterns.json, etc. | ~25MB | NEW |
| #1781 | Codex + Gemini state snapshots | Codex/Gemini | default.rules, history.jsonl, state.json, session export | ~350KB | NEW |
| #1583 | Hermes config parity | Hermes | config.yaml template, SOUL.md | existing | OPEN |
| #894 | Knowledge persistence architecture | All | WRK completion learnings, career knowledge | existing | OPEN |
| #194 | Codex session archive integration | Codex | Session JSONL export pipeline | existing | OPEN |
| #193 | Session scanner for historical learnings | Claude | Retroactive learning extraction | existing | OPEN |

## Implementation Order

1. **#1780** (fix nightly pipeline) — Lowest effort, highest impact. Just add `git add` + commit for files already allowed by .gitignore exceptions. ~25MB of corrections, patterns, insights immediately saved.

2. **#1778** (un-gitignore hermes state) — Add 7 gitignore exceptions + commit existing files. Hermes insights, cross-agent memory, drift summary, portfolio signals.

3. **#1779** (Claude project memory) — Snapshot 39 memory files (196KB). Most valuable per-byte: every `feedback_*.md` is a user correction.

4. **#1777** (Hermes memory) — Snapshot MEMORY.md + USER.md (3KB).

5. **#1781** (Codex + Gemini) — Snapshot rules, state, history. Build Codex session export pipeline.

6. **#1583** (config parity) — Already scoped, extends to ace-linux-2.

## Nightly Pipeline Changes (consolidated)

All snapshot + commit logic should be consolidated into ONE script called at the end of `comprehensive-learning-nightly.sh`:

```bash
scripts/cron/commit-learning-artifacts.sh
```

This script:
1. Snapshots agent memories (Hermes, Claude, Codex, Gemini) to `config/agents/*/`
2. `git add` all learning state directories
3. Runs `legal-sanity-scan.sh --diff-only` (MANDATORY before commit)
4. Commits and pushes if anything changed

## Legal Risk

Memory files and correction records can contain file paths, command strings, or project names that reference client work. ALL snapshot directories must be covered by `legal-sanity-scan.sh`. The commit script must fail-safe: if legal scan finds violations, skip the commit and log the issue.

## What a Fresh `git clone` Gets You After This

```
config/agents/
  hermes/memories/          # Hermes MEMORY.md + USER.md snapshots
  claude/memory-snapshots/  # 39 Claude project memory files
  codex/state-snapshots/    # default.rules + history.jsonl
  gemini/state-snapshots/   # state.json + projects.json

.claude/state/
  corrections/              # Error correction history
  patterns/                 # Learned behavioral patterns
  reflect-history/          # Self-reflection analysis
  cc-insights/              # Agent insights
  learned-patterns.json     # Distilled pattern database
  cc-user-insights.yaml     # User preference model
  hermes-insights.yaml      # Cross-agent Hermes export
  cross-agent-memory.yaml   # Unified memory index
  drift-summary.yaml        # Config/skill drift tracking
  portfolio-signals.yaml    # Repo health signals
  skill-eval-results/       # Skill evaluation scores

logs/orchestrator/hermes/   # Hermes session exports (JSONL)
logs/orchestrator/codex/    # Codex session exports (JSONL, future)
```

Total: ~40MB of institutional memory that survives machine loss.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All child issues closed
- [ ] `git clone` on a fresh machine + `sync-agent-configs.sh` restores all agent memories
- [ ] Nightly pipeline commits all learning artifacts without manual intervention
- [ ] Legal scan gates all committed learning data
- [ ] Session transcript rsync backup covers all 4 agents

issues.title: epic(repo-organization): canonical folder structure and refactor contract across tier-1 repos
issues.body:
## Summary
Create a dedicated follow-up issue for repo-wide structural refactors that are broader than code cleanup alone. The current tier-1 refactor umbrella (#1962) identifies architectural debt and duplicate patterns, but it does not yet break out a canonical folder-structure and repository-layout workstream.

## Why
Refactors keep stalling at the module/file level when the underlying repo shape is still inconsistent. The next pass should explicitly normalize repository anatomy so agents, humans, tests, CI, and future automation can navigate repos the same way.

This is especially important across tier-1 repos where differences in `src/` layout, test placement, docs organization, examples, fixtures, generated outputs, and archive boundaries create avoidable friction during implementation and review.

## Scope
Define and execute a repo-organization refactor contract across tier-1 repos, including:
- canonical top-level directory layout
- source/package placement (`src/` vs flat-package decision per repo, with migration guidance)
- test directory mirroring and fixture placement
- docs/knowledge/reference placement and archival boundaries
- scripts/tools/generated-artifact separation
- examples/demo/notebook/data-sample placement
- deprecation of legacy/duplicate folders
- import-surface and public-API stability rules during moves
- migration/redirect strategy for moved files and paths

## Deliverables
1. A scored inventory of current folder-structure drift across tier-1 repos.
2. A canonical repo-layout contract with allowed variations and anti-patterns.
3. A per-repo migration matrix showing:
   - current layout
   - target layout
   - breaking-risk level
   - path moves / redirects needed
4. Child execution issues for repos where structural migration should happen separately.
5. Validation checks to prevent regressions (for example path-policy checks, stale-path detection, docs reference checks, smoke tests).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] tier-1 repos have a documented target folder-structure contract
- [ ] current drift is inventoried by repo with concrete path-level findings
- [ ] structural work is separated into follow-up implementation issues instead of being buried in umbrella comments
- [ ] validation/guardrail checks are defined so future repo drift is detected automatically
- [ ] issue explicitly states which changes are safe renames vs breaking-path migrations

## Related
- #1962 Tier-1 Repo Ecosystem Refactoring
- #1567 Continuous Repo Architecture Intelligence
- #1603 Multi-repo architecture scan
- #84 aceengineer-admin repo restructure — canonical document taxonomy
- #1404 Organize /mnt/ace/docs/ subfolders and deduplicate engineering references

## Notes
This issue is intentionally about repository anatomy and navigation, not about individual feature implementations inside any one repo.

issues.title: feat(hermes): orchestrate AI provider usage and workstation dispatch
issues.body:
## Summary
Build and mature a Hermes-led orchestration flow that coordinates:

1. AI provider/model usage across Claude, Codex, Gemini, and future providers.
2. Work dispatch across network-accessible workstations, starting with `ace-linux-1` and `ace-linux-2` over VPN.
3. Queue/label/telemetry feedback so urgent expiring credits are consumed intentionally without breaking plan-first governance.

## Why now
- User priority on 2026-04-27: Codex credit is expiring in ~24 hours with ~50% remaining per user-visible subscription state; use it aggressively for bounded work before expiry.
- Existing workspace telemetry reports Codex as a high-priority execution lane (`docs/reports/provider-work-queue.md`), but this needs to be tied to workstation availability and Hermes orchestration decisions.
- Workstation priority is explicit: first `ace-linux-1`, then `ace-linux-2`, both VPN-accessible.

## Current evidence / anchors
- `docs/BUSINESS_BRAIN.md` lists `ace-linux-1` as primary Linux dev for daily AI work / Claude-Codex sessions, and `ace-linux-2` as secondary Linux dev for parallel AI work / overflow.
- `docs/BUSINESS_BRAIN.md` lists provider roles: Claude as default orchestrator, Codex as coding worker/adversarial reviewer, Gemini as narrow large-context research/review lane.
- `docs/reports/provider-work-queue.md` generated 2026-04-27 recommends provider order `gemini, codex, claude`, with Codex routing priority `highest` and several execution-ready Codex candidates.
- Live `scripts/ai/assessment/query-quota.sh --refresh --json` currently reports Codex from `history.jsonl`; this may conflict with user-visible expiring-credit state, so the plan must explicitly reconcile provider telemetry sources before trusting automation.

## Desired mature flow
Hermes should operate as the control-plane/orchestrator that can:

1. Refresh provider usage / quota telemetry and classify confidence per provider.
2. Inventory workstation availability, VPN reachability, repo sync health, and tool readiness for `ace-linux-1` and `ace-linux-2`.
3. Combine provider urgency + workstation readiness + issue status labels into a ranked dispatch plan.
4. Prefer Codex for the next 24 hours for bounded implementation, tests, cleanup, and mechanical issue execution where plans are already approved.
5. Preserve Claude for orchestration, plan synthesis, and adversarial review; preserve Gemini for batched research/recon where it fits.
6. Emit a reviewable dispatch ledger showing: issue, provider, workstation, reason, quota basis, safety gate, and expected validation.
7. Avoid unapproved implementation: only dispatch execution to issues with `status:plan-approved`, unless the dispatch task is planning/review-only.
8. Support manual override by the user before large batches or cross-machine operations.

## Initial scope proposal
This issue should first produce a canonical plan for a minimum viable orchestration flow, then proceed after approval.

In-scope candidates:
- Control-plane design for provider + workstation dispatch.
- Codex-expiry emergency routing playbook for the next 24 hours.
- Workstation readiness probes for `ace-linux-1` and `ace-linux-2`.
- Provider telemetry source-of-truth reconciliation.
- Dispatch ledger schema and operator-facing review packet.
- GitHub label/queue integration using existing `agent:*`, `machine:*`, `status:*`, `priority:*`, `cat:*`, and `domain:*` labels.

Out of scope unless split into child issues:
- Full distributed scheduler implementation across all machines.
- Secret distribution or credential synchronization beyond documented checks.
- Broad provider billing/account automation.
- Running unapproved repo mutations outside the plan-approved gate.

## Immediate Codex-expiry handling requirement
The plan should identify an immediate safe action path for the next 24 hours:

1. Refresh or reconcile Codex usage telemetry against the user-visible subscription state.
2. List `status:plan-approved` issues that are good Codex candidates.
3. Map the top candidates to `ace-linux-1` / `ace-linux-2` based on repo/worktree readiness.
4. Generate self-contained Codex prompts or Hermes/Codex launch commands.
5. Require final user approval before launching any long-running batch.

## Acceptance criteria
- A canonical plan artifact exists under `docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-issue-NNN-<slug>.md`.
- The plan includes resource intelligence from repo docs, provider utilization reports, label taxonomy, and workstation readiness evidence.
- The plan explicitly reconciles conflicting Codex usage telemetry sources.
- The plan defines the minimum viable dispatch ledger fields.
- The plan defines how `ace-linux-1` and `ace-linux-2` readiness is probed before assigning work.
- The plan defines routing rules for Claude / Codex / Gemini and explains the temporary Codex-first priority due to expiring credit.
- The plan identifies immediate plan-approved Codex work candidates or states why none are safe.
- Adversarial plan review is completed before the issue moves to `status:plan-review`.
- No implementation or cross-workstation dispatch starts until explicit user approval moves the issue to `status:plan-approved`.

## Suggested labels
- `enhancement`
- `priority:critical`
- `cat:ai-orchestration`
- `cat:harness`
- `domain:ai-orchestration`
- `domain:workstations`
- `domain:agent-cost-tracking`

## Related issues / context
- #2504 — dispatch-ledger trust contract and lease lifecycle writer.
- #2506 — Lane E implementation handoff readiness.
- #2408 — model-release readiness contract and upgrade playbook.
- #2301 — openai-codex transport/challenge recovery.

## Governance note
This is a planning-first issue. Implementation and cross-machine execution must follow the workspace gate:
Issue → resource intelligence → plan → adversarial review → `status:plan-review` → user approval → `status:plan-approved` → implementation/dispatch.

## Summary

Build a Codex-expiring-credit burn-down controller for Hermes orchestration. The controller should turn provider telemetry plus user-visible expiry/remaining-credit signals into a safe, useful queue of Codex-first work lanes while preserving plan gates and workstation readiness.

## Motivation

During #2519, the user reported Codex credit expiring in roughly 24 hours with about 50% usage remaining. The repo has provider telemetry artifacts, but the workflow still needs an operational layer that converts urgency into bounded, non-wasteful, plan-gated work rather than synthetic usage or unsafe over-dispatch.

## Scope

- Reconcile local telemetry artifacts with explicit user-visible provider expiry/remaining-credit signals.
- Rank Codex-fit work by:
  - `status:plan-approved` and local gate readiness,
  - `agent:codex` / provider routing score,
  - file/path contention risk,
  - validation cost and expected evidence quality,
  - workstation readiness (`ace-linux-1` control plane, `ace-linux-2` overflow).
- Produce a burn-down schedule that maintains useful parallel lanes without front-loading all usage.
- Include conservative fallback behavior when telemetry is stale, unavailable, or contradictory.
- Emit operator-ready prompts or launch-plan artifacts, but do not bypass approval gates.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given current provider queue artifacts, the controller can produce a ranked Codex burn-down plan with issue links and routing rationale.
- The plan distinguishes implementation-ready lanes from planning/review-only lanes.
- The plan explicitly states when `ace-linux-2` can execute work but cannot own GitHub mutation because of #2520.
- The controller records the source and confidence of quota/expiry inputs.
- No synthetic token burn is recommended; every lane must produce useful artifacts, fixes, reviews, or verification evidence.

## Related

- Parent: #2519
- Related: #1838 — AI credit utilization governance
- Related: #2520 — `ace-linux-2` GitHub auth blocker
- Provider queue artifacts: `config/ai-tools/provider-work-queue.json`, `docs/reports/provider-work-queue.md`

## Summary

Implement a machine-aware dispatch ledger and reconciliation loop for the continuous/parallel prompt flow created under #2519. The ledger should record which issue, provider, model, workstation, branch/worktree, evidence artifact, and GitHub authority owns each lane, then reconcile completion state without relying on memory or terminal scrollback.

## Motivation

The current two-machine prompt pack defines roles for `ace-linux-1` and `ace-linux-2`, but the durable state still depends on operator discipline. To mature the flow, Hermes needs a structured ledger that can survive context compaction, terminal restarts, and parallel worker handoffs.

## Scope

- Define a durable ledger schema for cross-workstation work lanes.
- Include required fields:
  - issue number / URL,
  - provider and model,
  - workstation and launch environment,
  - worktree/branch/path ownership,
  - approval/gate status,
  - expected validation command(s),
  - evidence artifact path,
  - GitHub mutation authority,
  - stop/fallback condition,
  - final status/verdict.
- Add a lightweight writer/updater script or documented CLI workflow.
- Add a reconciliation report that detects:
  - lanes with no evidence artifact,
  - completed work not commented to GitHub,
  - workers trying to mutate GitHub when auth is blocked,
  - file/path contention between active lanes,
  - stale plan-approved assumptions.
- Integrate with the machine prompts from `docs/plans/machine-prompts/2026-04-27/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- A control-plane Hermes session can create/update the ledger without needing hidden chat context.
- `ace-linux-2` lanes can write local result files while `ace-linux-1` remains GitHub mutation authority when `gh` auth is invalid.
- The ledger can be summarized into a morning/next-checkpoint report.
- Tests or fixture checks validate at least: open lane, completed lane, blocked lane, and GitHub-auth-blocked lane.
- The design references or reuses existing dispatch-ledger work instead of duplicating #2504.

## Related

- Related: #2504 — dispatch-ledger trust contract and lease lifecycle writer

issues.title: fix(workstations): repair and gate ace-linux-2 GitHub auth before delegation
issues.body:
## Summary
`ace-linux-2` currently has Hermes/Codex available in a login shell, but GitHub CLI auth is still invalid. Before delegating end-to-end issue execution to `ace-linux-2`, repair GH auth or constrain that workstation to local execution while `ace-linux-1` owns GitHub mutations.

## Evidence
Checked from `ace-linux-1` using login shell on `ace-linux-2`:

```bash
ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=8 ace-linux-2 'bash -lc '\''set +e; command -v gh; gh --version | head -3; gh auth status; gh api user --jq "{login:.login,id:.id}"'\'''
```

Observed:

```text
GH_PATH=/usr/bin/gh
gh version 2.90.0 (2026-04-16)

github.com
  X Failed to log in to github.com account vamseeachanta (default)
  - Active account: true
  - The token in default is invalid.
  - To re-authenticate, run: gh auth login -h github.com

GH_API_VIEWER
{
  "message": "Requires authentication",
  "documentation_url": "https://docs.github.com/rest",
  "status": "401"
}
gh: Requires authentication (HTTP 401)
```

## Why this matters
For #2519, `ace-linux-2` is intended as a high-priority overflow/Codex worker. It can run Hermes/Codex with `bash -lc`, but invalid GH auth blocks safe autonomous GitHub operations:

- issue comments
- label changes
- PR creation/review
- pushing through `gh` workflows
- closeout evidence posting

## Scope
Create or formalize a pre-delegation check script/runbook that validates `ace-linux-2` before launching workers.

Minimum checks:

1. SSH reachability via BatchMode.
2. Login-shell PATH includes Hermes/Codex:
   - `/home/vamsee/.local/bin/hermes`
   - `/home/vamsee/.npm-global/bin/codex`
3. Hermes model config confirms:
   - provider: `openai-codex`
   - model: `gpt-5.5`
4. Codex CLI exists and can report version.
5. GH auth is valid:
   - `gh auth status`
   - `gh api user --jq .login`
6. Canonical repo root exists:
   - `/mnt/local-analysis/workspace-hub`
7. Target tier-1 repo status is clean or has an approved dirty-state exception.
8. Engineering software smoke test, if the work packet requires a domain tool.

## Acceptance criteria
- A documented command or script exists to run the pre-delegation checks from `ace-linux-1` against `ace-linux-2`.
- The check clearly reports PASS/FAIL per capability: host, repo, Hermes, Codex, GH, engineering tools.
- #2519 can reference this as the mandatory gate before dispatching Codex/Hermes work to `ace-linux-2`.
- GH auth on `ace-linux-2` is either repaired and verified, or #2519 explicitly records that `ace-linux-1` retains GitHub mutation authority while `ace-linux-2` performs local execution only.

## Related
- Parent/control-plane issue: #2519
- Readiness probe artifact: `docs/reports/2026-04-27-issue-2519-ace-linux-2-readiness-probe.md`

issues.title: feat: review gate strict mode + GitHub Actions CI enforcement workflow
issues.body:
## Enable review gate strict mode and add GitHub Actions CI enforcement

### Current State
- require-review-on-push.sh exists but REVIEW_GATE_STRICT defaults to 0 (advisory)
- Pre-push hook calls review gate but only warns
- No GitHub Actions workflow for PR-level enforcement
- Compliance at 20% (improving from 4%)

### What Needs to Happen

**Phase 1: Enable Local Review Gate Strict Mode**
After plan gate is working (#2025), escalate:
```bash
# In .git/hooks/enforcement-env:
export REVIEW_GATE_STRICT=1
```
This will block pushes without cross-review evidence.

**Phase 2: GitHub Actions CI Workflow**
Create `.github/workflows/enforcement-gate.yml`:
```yaml
name: Enforcement Gate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  check-plan-approval:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Check Plan Approval
        run: bash scripts/enforcement/require-plan-approval.sh --strict
      - name: Check Review Evidence
        run: bash scripts/enforcement/require-review-on-push.sh HEAD $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)
  compliance-dashboard:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Run Compliance Check
        run: bash scripts/enforcement/compliance-dashboard.sh
```

**Phase 3: Progressive Rollout**
| Week | What | Risk |
|------|------|------|
| 1 | Plan gate strict (local only) | Low -- blocks obvious violations |
| 2 | Review gate strict (local only) | Medium -- may block legitimate work |
| 3 | CI workflow (PR level) | Medium -- external visibility |
| 4 | Full enforcement (all gates) | Low -- everything tested |

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] REVIEW_GATE_STRICT=1 in enforcement-env
- [ ] Push without review evidence is blocked
- [ ] GitHub Actions workflow created and passing
- [ ] PRs without plan approval are blocked by CI
- [ ] Compliance dashboard runs as CI step
- [ ] Bypass logging captures all override attempts

### Related
- vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2025 -- Plan gate strict mode and hook wiring
- vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1876 -- Enforcement infrastructure (parent)
- vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2017 -- Agent bypass resistance (metrics)

issues.title: Workflow hard-stops and session governance — Hermes-orchestrated lifecycle with enforced gates
issues.body:
## Problem

Our workflow lacks enforced hard stops where the user must review and approve before the agent continues. Evidence from session trend data is damning:

- **6.1M wasted tool calls** across 3 runaway WRK items (no session abort mechanism)
- **4,740 high-churn sessions** (100+ tool calls) with no ceiling
- **3% TDD pairing** vs "TDD mandatory" policy — the gate is aspirational, not enforced
- **12-day consecutive** smoke test failures went unnoticed
- **Review gate defaults to warning mode** — bypass trivial with `SKIP_REVIEW_GATE=1`
- **session-start-routine skill lost** during GSD migration cleanup
- **comprehensive-learning skill orphaned** from skills tree (runs via cron but invisible to skill discovery)

The old 20-stage WRK pipeline was removed (4% completion rate). The replacement 6-stage GSD workflow has quality gates but no session-level governance or mandatory user checkpoints.

## Current State

**What exists (stages/workflow):**
- 6-stage workflow: GitHub Issue → Triage → GSD Plan → Implement → Cross-Review → Close
- GSD framework with 56 workflow files (.claude/get-shit-done/workflows/)
- AGENTS.md hard gates: (1) Plan before acting, (2) TDD mandatory
- Trust Architecture doc (docs/governance/TRUST-ARCHITECTURE.md) — A/B/C action classification
- Pre-push review gate (warning mode by default)
- Self-learning loop: session signals → 3AM analysis → 5AM reflection
- Nightly comprehensive-learning pipeline (scripts/cron/)

**What exists (skills/docs):**
- agent-usage-optimizer skill (sub-skills all archived)
- AI_REVIEW_ROUTING_POLICY.md (3-provider adversarial review)
- work-queue-workflow.md (6-stage reference)
- 11 session handoff docs in docs/handoffs/

**What is missing:**
- No session hard-stop / tool-call ceiling — runaway sessions burn credits unchecked
- No mandatory user review checkpoint between Plan and Implement stages
- No session-start-routine skill (lost during migration)
- No session-corpus-audit capability (never built)
- No inter-session continuity gate (sessions dont validate prior state before starting new work)
- TDD gate not enforced via pre-commit hook
- comprehensive-learning disconnected from skill tree
- cross-review-policy, dev-workflow, codex-review, gemini-review skills referenced but never created

## Proposal: Hermes-Orchestrated Workflow with Hard Stops

### Phase 1: Session Lifecycle Gates

**Mandatory User Hard Stops (cannot be bypassed):**

```
SESSION START
  ├─ [GATE 1: Session Init] Auto — load context, check prior state, validate env
  │
  ├─ [GATE 2: Work Selection] Auto — triage issues, present options
  │
  ├─ [HARD STOP 1: Plan Approval] ◆ USER MUST APPROVE plan before any implementation
  │
  ├─ [GATE 3: TDD Red] Auto — tests written, all failing (enforced, not advisory)
  │
  ├─ [GATE 4: Implementation] Auto — make tests pass
  │
  ├─ [GATE 5: Cross-Review] Auto — route to Codex+Gemini per routing policy
  │
  ├─ [HARD STOP 2: Review Verdict] ◆ USER REVIEWS cross-review results, approves/rejects
  │
  ├─ [GATE 6: Commit+Push] Auto — commit, push, close issue
  │
  └─ [HARD STOP 3: Session Close] ◆ USER CONFIRMS session summary, next priorities
SESSION END
```

3 hard stops per session. Everything else is automated by Hermes.

### Phase 2: Runaway Protection

- **Tool-call ceiling**: Auto-pause at 200 tool calls, require user confirmation to continue
- **Time ceiling**: Auto-pause after 45 minutes of continuous work, present progress summary
- **Error loop breaker**: If same error repeats 3x, hard stop — do not retry
- **Credit guard**: Pause if estimated session cost exceeds threshold (ties to #1838)

### Phase 3: Restore Lost Infrastructure

- Rebuild `session-start-routine` skill with: pre-flight checks, context loading, prior-state validation, tool readiness
- Create `session-corpus-audit` skill: analyze session quality trends, identify high-churn patterns, report waste
- Promote `comprehensive-learning` into skills tree (currently cron-only, invisible)
- Create `cross-review-policy` skill (policy exists as doc, not as actionable skill)
- Create `dev-workflow` skill encapsulating the full Issue→Close lifecycle

### Phase 4: Hermes as Workflow Orchestrator

Hermes (not Claude Code directly) orchestrates the session lifecycle:
- Hermes manages gate transitions and hard-stop enforcement
- Hermes dispatches to Claude/Codex/Gemini per routing matrix (#1838)
- Hermes tracks session metrics (tool calls, time, credits, gate pass/fail)
- Hermes generates session report at close (ties to gsd-session-report)
- Inter-session continuity: Hermes checks last session state before starting new work

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] 3 mandatory user hard stops implemented and non-bypassable
- [ ] Tool-call ceiling (200) with auto-pause operational
- [ ] TDD gate enforced via pre-commit hook (not advisory)
- [ ] session-start-routine skill rebuilt and active
- [ ] session-corpus-audit skill created
- [ ] comprehensive-learning promoted to skill tree
- [ ] Review gate defaults to strict mode (not warning)
- [ ] Hermes session report generated at every session close
- [ ] Zero runaway sessions (>500 tool calls) in first month
- [ ] Inter-session state validation before new work begins

## References

- docs/reports/session-failures-and-refactor-review.md (6.1M wasted calls analysis)
- docs/governance/TRUST-ARCHITECTURE.md (A/B/C action classification)
- docs/work-queue-workflow.md (6-stage canonical workflow)
- docs/standards/AI_REVIEW_ROUTING_POLICY.md
- docs/reports/review-gate-strict-mode-evaluation-2026-04-03.md
- notes/gatepass-weekly-summary.md (gate-start skipping evidence)
- Related: #1838 (credit utilization), #1805 (security kill switches), #1775 (CC best practices)
- Closed predecessors: #440 (trust architecture), #1065 (gate+logging), #816 (review stages), #1061 (workflow hardening)

issues.title: feat(harness): weekly Claude Code best-practice adoption cadence — 8-week plan from shanraisshan/claude-code-best-practice
issues.body:
## Context

Review of [shanraisshan/claude-code-best-practice](https://github.com/shanraisshan/claude-code-best-practice) (133k+ stars, updated for CC v2.1.90) revealed significant gaps between native Claude Code capabilities and our ecosystem usage. This issue tracks an 8-week adoption cadence.

**Key finding:** `/powerup` and `/insights` are NATIVE CC commands (not custom). We have been reinventing wheels instead of leveraging built-in features. See vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1760 comment for details.

**Source repo cloned to:** `/tmp/claude-code-best-practice` (reference)

---

## 8-Week Adoption Cadence

### Week 1: Native Command Literacy
**Goal:** Every developer runs /powerup once, team adopts /insights + /stats + /context

- [ ] Run `/powerup` on all machines (dev-primary, dev-secondary) — complete all 10 lessons
- [ ] Run `/insights` and review session analysis report; compare with our custom pipeline output
- [ ] Run `/stats` to establish baseline usage patterns
- [ ] Run `/context` at mid-session to understand context budget consumption
- [ ] Document findings in `docs/superpowers/reports/week-1-native-commands.md`
- [ ] Add `/context` at 50% as a session discipline rule to CLAUDE.md ("compact at max 50%")

### Week 2: settings.json Modernization
**Goal:** Leverage native CC settings we are ignoring

- [ ] Configure `statusLine` — show context %, model, rate limits, git branch
- [ ] Configure `spinnerVerbs` and `spinnerTipsOverride` with ecosystem-specific tips
- [ ] Set `outputStyle: "Explanatory"` for insight boxes during development
- [ ] Set `effortLevel` appropriately (opus=high for planning, sonnet=medium for code)
- [ ] Configure `plansDirectory` to route to our `.planning/` directory
- [ ] Configure `worktree.symlinkDirectories` for `node_modules`, `.cache`
- [ ] Add `$schema` for IDE validation: `"https://json.schemastore.org/claude-code-settings.json"`
- [ ] Review and set `autoMode` rules for trusted operations
- [ ] Document in `docs/superpowers/reports/week-2-settings.md`

### Week 3: Hooks Infrastructure
**Goal:** Implement the 3 high-value hook patterns from best-practice repo

- [ ] **PreToolUse hook** — measure skill usage frequency (which skills fire, how often)
  - Log to `.claude/state/skill-usage.jsonl`
  - Surface in nightly comprehensive-learning pipeline
- [ ] **PostToolUse hook** — auto-format on Edit/Write (ruff format for .py, prettier for .md/.yaml)
  - Only trigger on file-modifying tools
  - Must be < 2 seconds per invocation
- [ ] **Stop hook** — verification nudge at end of turn
  - Prompt: "Did you verify the output? Did you run tests?"
  - Light touch — raw signal write, no blocking
- [ ] Wire hooks into `.claude/settings.json` (project-scoped)
- [ ] Test on dev-primary, verify no performance regression
- [ ] Document in `docs/superpowers/reports/week-3-hooks.md`

### Week 4: Skills Modernization (Batch 1 — Top 20)
**Goal:** Upgrade 20 most-used skills with native CC frontmatter fields

- [ ] Audit top 20 skills by usage (from Week 3 hook data, or git log frequency)
- [ ] Add native frontmatter fields to each:
  - `context: fork` for isolated execution where appropriate
  - `paths` for auto-discovery triggers (e.g., OrcaFlex skill fires on .dat/.yml files)
  - `model` and `effort` overrides (haiku for fast lookup, opus for planning)
  - `hooks` scoped to skill (e.g., /careful blocks destructive commands)
- [ ] Add `## Gotchas` section to each skill (failure points learned over time)
- [ ] Add `## Progressive Disclosure` structure (references/, scripts/, examples/ subdirs)
- [ ] Ensure skill `description` is written as trigger ("when should I fire?") not summary
- [ ] Document in `docs/superpowers/reports/week-4-skills-modernization.md`

### Week 5: Native Agent Definitions (.claude/agents/)
**Goal:** Create 5 core agents using native CC agent format

- [ ] **engineering-explorer** — model:haiku, tools:Read-only, for fast codebase search
  - Skills preloaded: repo-structure, ecosystem-terminology
- [ ] **orcaflex-specialist** — model:opus, skills:orcaflex+orcawave, color:green
  - Preloaded domain knowledge, isolation:worktree for parallel runs
- [ ] **code-reviewer** — model:opus, effort:high, skills:code-review+clean-code
  - Stop hook for review verdict enforcement
- [ ] **overnight-planner** — model:opus, effort:high, background:true
  - Skills: overnight-parallel-agent-prompts, cross-review-policy
  - initialPrompt with session-start context load
- [ ] **data-pipeline** — model:sonnet, skills:data-analysis+xlsx+pdf
  - paths: "*.csv,*.xlsx,*.pdf" for auto-activation
- [ ] Place in `.claude/agents/` directory (native CC format)
- [ ] Document in `docs/superpowers/reports/week-5-agents.md`

### Week 6: Command→Agent→Skill Orchestration
**Goal:** Build 3 orchestration commands following the pattern from best-practice repo

- [ ] **`/workspace-health`** — Command orchestrates:
  1. Spawns `engineering-explorer` agent to scan repo health
  2. Invokes `repo-capability-map` skill for analysis
  3. Invokes `interactive-report-generator` skill for HTML output
- [ ] **`/orcaflex-pipeline`** — Command orchestrates:
  1. Spawns `orcaflex-specialist` agent to parse .dat files
  2. Invokes `orcaflex-enrichment` skill for YAML conversion
  3. Invokes `plotly-visualization` skill for results
- [ ] **`/daily-brief`** — Command orchestrates:
  1. Runs native `/insights` for session analysis
  2. Spawns agent to check GitHub issues + PR status
  3. Invokes `today` skill for priority recommendations
- [ ] Place in `.claude/commands/` directory
- [ ] Document orchestration pattern in `docs/superpowers/reports/week-6-orchestration.md`

### Week 7: Self-Improvement Commands (#1760)
**Goal:** Wire the self-improvement commands from vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1760

- [ ] `/improve` — lightweight ad-hoc mode (standalone, < 30s)
- [ ] `/compound` — wire compound-engineering skill to command entry
- [ ] `/reflect` — wire claude-reflect skill to command entry
- [ ] `/knowledge` — implement knowledge capture/retrieval command
- [ ] Update `config/workflow-tips/tips-catalog.yaml` with correct try_it paths
- [ ] Verify nightly comprehensive-learning pipeline still works unchanged
- [ ] Document in `docs/superpowers/reports/week-7-self-improvement.md`

### Week 8: Cross-Model Review + Squash Discipline
**Goal:** Enforce the workflow patterns from Boris Cherny tips

- [ ] Enforce squash merge on all PRs (configure GitHub repo settings)
- [ ] Set PR size target: p50 < 150 lines (add to CLAUDE.md as rule)
- [ ] Implement cross-model review: Claude plan → Codex review → Gemini audit
  - Wire to existing cross-review-policy skill
  - Add as mandatory gate in GSD workflow
- [ ] Add `/compact` at 50% context as a CLAUDE.md rule
- [ ] Add `/rename` discipline for important sessions
- [ ] Final report: `docs/superpowers/reports/week-8-workflow-discipline.md`

---

## Weekly Execution Pattern

Each week follows the same ritual:

```
Monday:    Read the week focus above. Plan specific files/configs to change.
Tue-Thu:   Implement changes. Use /powerup lessons if stuck on CC features.
Friday:    Write the weekly report in docs/superpowers/reports/week-N-*.md
           Run /insights + /stats to measure impact.
           Commit + push all changes.
```

## Success Metrics (measured at Week 8)

| Metric | Baseline (now) | Target |
|--------|---------------|--------|
| Native CC features actively used | ~3 (/plan, /compact, /model) | 15+ |
| Skills with native frontmatter (context, paths, effort) | 0 | 20+ |
| .claude/agents/ definitions | 0 | 5+ |
| Orchestration commands (Command→Agent→Skill) | 0 | 3+ |
| Hooks active (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop) | 0 | 3 |
| settings.json features leveraged | ~5 | 15+ |
| Self-improvement commands wired | 0 | 4+ (/improve, /compound, /reflect, /knowledge) |
| Average PR size (lines) | unmeasured | p50 < 150 |

## Related Issues

issues.title: fix(provider-telemetry): improve Claude and Gemini quota observability for exact weekly targeting
issues.body:
## Summary
Improve Claude and Gemini quota observability so provider utilization can support exact weekly targeting instead of falling back to directional activity heuristics.

## Why
The current routing/control-plane stack is useful, but quota observability is still the limiting factor for precise weekly credit optimization:
- Claude quota is still frequently `source: unavailable`
- Gemini quota is still `source: estimated`
- utilization reports therefore fall back to activity-vs-recent-peak for two key providers

This means the system can route work intelligently, but cannot yet guarantee near-100% weekly usage with high confidence.

## Scope
- identify stronger live data sources for Claude weekly headroom
- identify stronger live data sources for Gemini usage/headroom
- wire improved sources into query-quota / latest quota artifacts
- preserve current fallback behavior when better telemetry is unavailable
- update reports to distinguish exact vs estimated weekly targeting confidence

## Deliverables
- improved quota-source extraction or parsing for Claude/Gemini
- updated quota snapshot artifacts
- utilization report notes showing confidence level per provider
- tests for the new telemetry paths and fallback behavior

## Related
- Parent provider-utilization strategy: #1838
- Weekly provider review context: #2089
- Existing quota/cache hygiene issues: #2108, #2109

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Claude quota source is stronger than `unavailable` in the normal healthy path
- [ ] Gemini usage source is stronger than `estimated` in the normal healthy path
- [ ] utilization reports can distinguish exact vs heuristic routing confidence
- [ ] fallback behavior remains safe when direct telemetry is unavailable

issues.title: feat(doc-intel): materialize wiki_refs reverse lookup from doc_key to citing wiki pages
issues.body:
## Summary
Materialize the `wiki_refs` reverse-lookup contract that is already defined in the provenance architecture, so a registry entry or `doc_key` can answer: which LLM-wiki pages cite this source?

## Why
Repo review surfaced a concrete cross-layer gap:
- `docs/document-intelligence/intelligence-accessibility-map.md` says there is currently no reverse lookup from registry/doc_key -> affected wiki pages.
- `docs/document-intelligence/standards-codes-provenance-reuse-contract.md` already defines `wiki_refs` as the L2 materialized back-link field and calls out `scripts/knowledge/llm_wiki.py` as the place to emit it.
- Today, when a source document is updated, reclassified, or deduplicated, downstream wiki impact has to be found with grep.

This blocks trustworthy maintenance of 19k+ wiki pages and weakens the repo ecosystem's ability to propagate standards/document changes into durable knowledge.

## Grounding
- LLM-wiki counts currently observed in repo: engineering 83, marine-engineering 19184, maritime-law 22, naval-architecture 45, personal 5.
- `docs/document-intelligence/intelligence-accessibility-map.md` classifies missing registry backlinks from wikis as an active weak accessibility pattern.
- `docs/document-intelligence/standards-codes-provenance-reuse-contract.md` Section 4.3 + implementation notes already specify `wiki_refs` semantics.

## Scope
- Add a concrete reverse-lookup materialization path from L3 wiki page citations into L2 registries/ledgers.
- Define which registry surfaces get `wiki_refs` first (at minimum the standards-transfer ledger and primary document-index registry surfaces).
- Update `scripts/knowledge/llm_wiki.py` ingest/update flow to emit or refresh `wiki_refs` when wiki pages are created/updated.
- Add a query path/script for `doc_key -> wiki pages` lookup.
- Add regression tests/fixtures for pages being added, updated, removed, or changing cited `doc_key` values.

## Deliverables
- Implementation plan for first-class `wiki_refs` materialization.
- Reverse-lookup command or helper with deterministic output.
- Tests proving add/update/delete behavior keeps `wiki_refs` truthful.
- Migration/backfill strategy for pre-existing wiki pages.
- Documentation showing how issue planning and wiki maintenance should use the reverse lookup.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] given a `doc_key`, the repo can return all citing wiki pages without grep
- [ ] back-links stay correct when a wiki page changes cited sources
- [ ] pre-existing wiki pages have a bounded backfill path
- [ ] at least one L2 registry/ledger surface stores `wiki_refs` in a durable/queryable way
- [ ] docs explain the L3->L2 back-link materialization rule

## Related
- Parent operating model: vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2205
- Provenance/reuse contract: vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2207
- Cross-wiki/linking work: vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#36, vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#35, vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2068
- Frontmatter/doc_key follow-ons: vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2233, vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#23, vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2362

- Define required Lane E handoff fields: issue, PR/branch, dispatch/routine id, plan SHA, approval marker/evidence, changed files, tests/CI, artifacts, risks, implementation-review status, recommended human action, review effort, and priority reason.

- Performing implementation code review itself.
- Merging PRs.
- Creating dispatch leases.

{"issues": [{"url": "https://github.com/vamseeachanta/llm-wiki/issues/26", "title": "feat(knowledge): execute Batch Pack 4 for non-ACMA standards summary promotion", "issue_number": 26, "body": "## Summary
Execute Batch Pack 4 as a narrowly scoped, summary-backed promotion wave for non-ACMA standards knowledge in cathodic-protection, pipeline, and structural domains.

## Why
Parallel repo review found that this is the strongest remaining designed batch-pack opportunity:
- `docs/reports/llm-wiki-external-source-priority-queue.md` and the YAML queue rank standards-with-existing-summaries as the next major promotion family.
- `data/document-index/resource-intelligence-maturity.yaml` reports 639,585 existing summaries and 425 standards in active maturity scope.
- This work can promote existing L2 evidence into L3 wiki knowledge without rereading source PDFs.

The key is to scope it carefully so it complements, rather than duplicates, ACMA/OCIMF/CSA or design-code-registry work.

## Scope
- Use only existing summary-backed and ledger-backed evidence.
- Start with non-ACMA domains/sub-slices: cathodic-protection, pipeline, and structural.
- Generate topic/domain stubs and cross-links from existing summary + ledger data.
- Explicitly exclude:
  - ACMA/naval-architecture/OCIMF/CSA-specific promotion already covered by vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2216 / vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2227 / vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2284
  - design-code-registry family overviews/backlinks covered by vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#31
  - raw source-PDF rereads

## Deliverables
- Batch Pack 4 execution artifact/report for the chosen non-ACMA domains.
- Summary-backed wiki-ready topic/domain stubs.
- Duplicate/extend-vs-create map against existing standards/wiki pages.
- Provenance references back to the transfer ledger and summary sources.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] promotion uses existing summary/ledger evidence only
- [ ] first slice is limited to cathodic-protection, pipeline, and structural domains
- [ ] ACMA/design-code-registry scope is explicitly excluded to avoid duplication
- [ ] outputs include extend-vs-create and provenance mapping, not raw dump notes

Execute the already-designed external-source Batch Pack 1 so the repo promotes metadata-rich online data APIs and standards portals into wiki-ready stubs for the thin LLM-wiki domains.

- engineering wiki: 83 pages
- naval-architecture wiki: 45 pages
- maritime-law wiki: 22 pages
- marine-engineering wiki: 19,184 pages

At the same time, the repo already has a prepared execution design:

- [ ] each output stub has a clear target wiki domain and provenance reference
- [ ] duplicate targets are identified before promotion

## Context
Metadata-only discovery of `/mnt/ace-data` raw-like stores identified several high-value offshore/energy source families that are not directly covered by existing llm-wiki completion plans:

- `/mnt/ace-data/client_projects/energy_bsee/raw_data` — 10 files (PDF/XLSX/DOCX/ZIP), BSEE/offshore well data descriptions and sample permit/activity material.
- `/mnt/ace-data/worldenergydata/data/modules/hse/raw` — 97 files / 7 dirs, OSHA/HSE CSV/TXT/ZIP datasets and metadata.
- `/mnt/ace-data/frontierdeepwater/data/raw` — 4 files / 1 dir, offshore magazine/heavy-lift/pipelay source material.

Focused duplicate searches found no direct open issue for `energy_bsee raw_data`, `worldenergydata hse llm-wiki`, or `frontierdeepwater llm-wiki`. Existing adjacent anchors remain vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#13 (roadmap), vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2392 (coverage-gap detector), and vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2487 (raw-data-to-readiness spine).

## Problem
These offshore/energy raw-source families may contain useful llm-wiki completion signals for engineering, marine-engineering, HSE/safety, drilling, production, and offshore operations domains, but they must be handled carefully:

- only metadata and derived summaries may be promoted;
- client/project-sensitive files require separate approval;
- raw data and proprietary files must remain mounted-source only;
- source-family package boundaries must be approved before any extraction/backfill work.

## Scope
Create an approval-ready canonical plan that defines bounded source-family packages for:
1. BSEE/offshore source metadata and summary candidates,
2. HSE/safety dataset metadata and wiki concept/source candidates, and
3. Frontier Deepwater/offshore operations source candidates.

The plan should produce a safe, reviewable execution route after approval, including target wiki domains, expected summary/page types, exclusions, tests/checks, and provenance gates.

## Out of scope
- No raw data copying into git/wiki.
- No direct extraction from client-sensitive files without separate approval.
- No website/GTM artifact generation.
- No AQWA/OrcaFlex/O&G standards work here; those map to existing issues (#2103, vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2124, vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#25/#2373/standards waves) or the raw-like routing issue.
- No implementation before canonical plan review and user approval.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A canonical plan is created under `docs/plans/` and indexed in `docs/plans/README.md`.
- [ ] The plan includes a source-family matrix with BSEE, HSE, and Frontier Deepwater candidates, target wiki domains, exclusion rules, provenance requirements, and follow-up package sequencing.
- [ ] The plan cites metadata-only inventory evidence and focused duplicate-search evidence showing no direct duplicate issue for these three families.
- [ ] The plan defines approval gates for any raw/project-sensitive material before summary promotion.
- [ ] The final plan-review comment requests user approval and labels this issue `status:plan-review`.

# feat(llm-wiki): plan offshore raw-source family wiki backfill candidates from /mnt/ace-data

## Context
Metadata-only discovery of `/mnt/ace-data` raw-like stores identified several high-value offshore/energy source families that are not directly covered by existing llm-wiki completion plans:

- `/mnt/ace-data/client_projects/energy_bsee/raw_data` — 10 files (PDF/XLSX/DOCX/ZIP), BSEE/offshore well data descriptions and sample permit/activity material.
- `/mnt/ace-data/worldenergydata/data/modules/hse/raw` — 97 files / 7 dirs, OSHA/HSE CSV/TXT/ZIP datasets and metadata.
- `/mnt/ace-data/frontierdeepwater/data/raw` — 4 files / 1 dir, offshore magazine/heavy-lift/pipelay source material.

Focused duplicate searches found no direct open issue for `energy_bsee raw_data`, `worldenergydata hse llm-wiki`, or `frontierdeepwater llm-wiki`. Existing adjacent anchors remain vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#13 (roadmap), vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2392 (coverage-gap detector), and vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2487 (raw-data-to-readiness spine).

## Problem
These offshore/energy raw-source families may contain useful llm-wiki completion signals for engineering, marine-engineering, HSE/safety, drilling, production, and offshore operations domains, but they must be handled carefully:

- only metadata and derived summaries may be promoted;
- client/project-sensitive files require separate approval;
- raw data and proprietary files must remain mounted-source only;
- source-family package boundaries must be approved before any extraction/backfill work.

## Scope
Create an approval-ready canonical plan that defines bounded source-family packages for:
1. BSEE/offshore source metadata and summary candidates,
2. HSE/safety dataset metadata and wiki concept/source candidates, and
3. Frontier Deepwater/offshore operations source candidates.

The plan should produce a safe, reviewable execution route after approval, including target wiki domains, expected summary/page types, exclusions, tests/checks, and provenance gates.

## Out of scope
- No raw data copying into git/wiki.
- No direct extraction from client-sensitive files without separate approval.
- No website/GTM artifact generation.
- No AQWA/OrcaFlex/O&G standards work here; those map to existing issues (#2103, vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2124, vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#25/#2373/standards waves) or the raw-like routing issue.
- No implementation before canonical plan review and user approval.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A canonical plan is created under `docs/plans/` and indexed in `docs/plans/README.md`.
- [ ] The plan includes a source-family matrix with BSEE, HSE, and Frontier Deepwater candidates, target wiki domains, exclusion rules, provenance requirements, and follow-up package sequencing.
- [ ] The plan cites metadata-only inventory evidence and focused duplicate-search evidence showing no direct duplicate issue for these three families.
- [ ] The plan defines approval gates for any raw/project-sensitive material before summary promotion.
- [ ] The final plan-review comment requests user approval and labels this issue `status:plan-review`.

issues.title: Research: reservoir engineering literature — local /mnt/ace + online; ingest to llm-wiki
issues.body:
## Goal

Build out the reservoir-engineering substrate of llm-wiki by mining (a) the user's existing local PDF corpus on ace-linux-1 (`/mnt/ace`, 30,499 PDFs) and (b) public online sources, then ingesting the relevant material under llm-wiki's MIT + CC-BY-4.0 license. Drives both the [Kaggle ROGII Wellbore Geology Prediction](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/kaggle-rogii-2026) competition (deeper domain literacy → better modeling decisions) and longer-term wikis around oil & gas / subsurface engineering.

Companion issue: [vamseeachanta/kaggle-rogii-2026#5](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/kaggle-rogii-2026/issues/5) covers competition-specific *prior art* (datasets + ML papers); this issue covers the broader *educational foundation* (textbooks, coursework, classic papers).

## Scope

**In-scope source types**

- Textbooks on reservoir engineering, petroleum engineering, formation evaluation, well logging, drilling, geosteering.
- University coursework — open syllabi, lecture notes, problem sets from Stanford SDSS, Texas A&M, U Texas Austin, Heriot-Watt, IFP, Imperial.
- Conference papers — SPE, AAPG, SEG, EAGE — with care about open-access vs paywalled.
- Industry standards / methodology PDFs (DNV, API, ISO).
- Theses and dissertations from public university repositories.
- ArXiv preprints in petroleum engineering, geophysics, ML-for-geosteering categories.

**Out of scope (license / IP risk)**

- Pirated or unauthorized copies of paywalled textbooks, even if found locally.
- Vendor-derivative material under proprietary license.
- The deny-list per [vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2482](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2482) governance: nothing under `knowledge/wikis/*/wiki/sources/` should be cited; cite the canonical standard or concept page instead.

## Sources to mine

### Local — `/mnt/ace` (ace-linux-1)

- `/mnt/ace/rock-oil-field/` — top candidate directory by name. First pass: recursively list, classify by filename / metadata, flag candidates.
- `/mnt/ace/aceengineer-admin/Reference/` — mixed (mostly tax / admin docs in spot-check, but may contain technical references).
- Other dirs revealed during initial sweep.
- Total PDFs in `/mnt/ace`: ~30,499. Realistic target: 50–200 ingest-worthy after deduplication and license filtering.

### Online (representative starting points)

- **Stanford Stanford Doerr School OCW**: open courses on petroleum / energy resources.
- **Texas A&M PETE OCW** and **U Texas Austin Petroleum Engineering** open content.
- **Heriot-Watt PE** open materials.
- **arXiv physics.geo-ph** and **stat.ML** intersection — search "well log", "geosteering", "lithology classification".
- **OnePetro** free-access entries (SPE / AAPG / SEG; many old papers are now open).
- **AAPG Datapages** open-access portion.
- **USGS Open-File Reports** in petroleum geology.
- **OAPEN** and **Springer Open** for free textbooks.
- **MIT OpenCourseWare** earth-and-planetary courses with subsurface relevance.

## Output: llm-wiki structure

Existing top-level dirs (verified 2026-05-06): `docs/`, `scripts/`, `seeds/`, `tests/`, `wikis/`.

Proposed additions / extensions (subject to existing wiki conventions; defer final layout to whoever owns llm-wiki structure decisions):

- `wikis/reservoir-engineering/` (new, if not present) with:
  - `concepts/` — fundamentals: porosity, permeability, saturation, capillary pressure, relative permeability, etc.
  - `methodology/` — geosteering workflow, reservoir characterization, log interpretation, formation evaluation.
  - `standards/` — DNV / API / ISO references with [#2471](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2471)-shape frontmatter (`code_id`, `publisher`, `revision`).
  - `sources/` — citation index, NOT ingestion targets per [vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2482](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2482).
- `docs/research/reservoir-engineering-corpus.md` — log of every source examined, decision (ingest / skip / defer), license note.

## Workflow

1. **Local sweep.** Inventory `/mnt/ace/rock-oil-field/` and other candidate dirs. Output: a manifest of `(filepath, size, page-count, title-from-metadata, classification)` rows. ~1 hr scripted.
2. **Online sweep.** 6–10 best-of-class courses, textbooks (open-access only), and survey papers. Bookmark + brief description. ~1–2 hr.
3. **License triage.** Drop everything that's not clearly redistributable. Prefer creative-commons or public-domain (older works > 70 yrs).
4. **Wiki page drafts.** Write 5–15 concept pages (`wikis/reservoir-engineering/concepts/*.md`) in llm-wiki's existing style. Cite sources, never copy. Apply the calc-citation contract (`workspace-hub/.claude/rules/calc-citation-contract.md`) where formulas appear.
5. **PR with the corpus + wiki pages + citation log.** Reviewer checks license, citation, and that copy is original (not paraphrased > 30-word chunks).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `/mnt/ace` reservoir-engineering inventory at `docs/research/reservoir-engineering-corpus.md` lists at least 50 candidate sources with classification (ingest / skip / defer) and license note.
- [ ] At least 5 concept pages drafted under `wikis/reservoir-engineering/concepts/` covering core fundamentals (porosity, permeability, gamma-ray log interpretation, dip / azimuth, formation tops).
- [ ] At least 2 methodology pages under `wikis/reservoir-engineering/methodology/` covering geosteering workflow + log correlation.
- [ ] All cited sources licensed for redistribution OR cited only as reference (no in-page copying).
- [ ] PR opened, reviewed, merged with the standard llm-wiki review process.
- [ ] Cross-link added to [vamseeachanta/kaggle-rogii-2026#5](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/kaggle-rogii-2026/issues/5) when the wiki pages are ready, so Kaggle modeling work can reference them.

## Risks and open questions

- **Risk:** `/mnt/ace/rock-oil-field/` may contain user-purchased textbooks not licensed for redistribution. Triage carefully — local-use-only OK, ingestion-to-public-repo NOT OK.
- **Open:** Should reservoir-engineering wiki pages live under a top-level `wikis/reservoir-engineering/` or inside the existing marine/offshore family? Defer to llm-wiki maintainer decision.
- **Open:** What citation style — IEEE-numeric, APA, or the inline `code_id` style from [#2471](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2471)? Likely match the existing llm-wiki convention.

## Time budget

A few sessions across 1–2 weeks. Don't disappear into a literature rabbit hole; the 50-source target keeps it bounded.

## Summary
Backfill promotion provenance on pre-existing wiki pages so older LLM-wiki content can answer what source artifact, issue, seed, or registry record it was promoted from.

## Why
Parallel repo review found that the policy stack now expects stronger provenance, but much of the existing wiki corpus predates that discipline:
- the provenance contract defines richer `doc_key`/promotion semantics
- new work is adding `doc_key` and `wiki_refs` capabilities (#2363, vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#23, vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2362)
- older wiki pages and logs still often lack page-level promotion lineage, which weakens maintenance and reuse

Without provenance backfill, older pages remain hard to audit when source docs, issues, or registries change.

## Scope

## Summary

- 19,137 of those pages use filename-style titles like `spe143317.pdf`.
- 1,458 use purely numeric titles like `22035.pdf`.

## Scope

- Derive `canonical_title` / `title_aliases` / equivalent display metadata from existing L2 evidence where available (conference metadata, summaries, registry titles, extracted titles).

- Update index/search generation to prefer human-readable titles while preserving stable links.

issues.title: feat(knowledge): update wiki CLAUDE.md files to declare doc_key in L3 frontmatter required-set
issues.body:
## Context

Parent vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2205 operating model Section 8.1 (amendment 2026-04-19, [comment](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2205#issuecomment-4277238819)) mandates a baseline floor of `{title, last_updated, doc_key}` as required fields in every wiki `CLAUDE.md` schema declaration. No wiki `CLAUDE.md` currently declares `doc_key` as required.

This blocks the vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2206 FRONT-1 conformance check from being enforced without day-one failures.

## Current state (verified 2026-04-19)

| Wiki | `CLAUDE.md` path | Current required-set | Missing from baseline floor |
|---|---|---|---|
| engineering | `knowledge/wikis/engineering/CLAUDE.md` | `{title, tags, added, last_updated}` | `doc_key` |
| maritime-law | `knowledge/wikis/maritime-law/CLAUDE.md` (if present) | uses `{domain, created, last_updated, page_count}` in index | `title`, `doc_key` |
| naval-architecture | `knowledge/wikis/naval-architecture/CLAUDE.md` (if present) | uses `{domain, created, last_updated, page_count}` in index | `title`, `doc_key` |
| _other wikis_ | per-wiki `CLAUDE.md` | varies | all must add `doc_key` |

## Scope

1. Audit every `knowledge/wikis/*/CLAUDE.md` file.
2. For each, update the required-set declaration to include all three baseline-floor fields: `title`, `last_updated`, `doc_key`.
3. Preserve domain-specific required fields already in place.
4. For wikis lacking a `CLAUDE.md`, decide whether to create one (likely yes for any wiki with governed L3 content).
5. Update existing L3 pages that lack `doc_key` — either backfill from the registry or add a grace-period transition policy.

## Out of scope

- Changing the baseline floor itself (locked by parent Section 8.1).
- Implementing the FRONT-1 conformance check in code (separate issue under vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2206).
- Per-child contract fields (#2207, vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2209 own those).

## References

- Parent operating model: `docs/document-intelligence/llm-wiki-resource-doc-intelligence-operating-model.md` §8.1
- Parent amendment summary: [#2205 comment 4277238819](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2205#issuecomment-4277238819)

## Related

- Depends on: vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2205 (amendment is authoritative)
- Blocks: vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2206 FRONT-1 check enforcement
- Related: vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2207 §6.3 (adds provenance fields on top of baseline), vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2209 §10.1 (adds durability fields on top of baseline)

## Acceptance criteria

## Summary

Tier C added ~75 new wiki pages across 6 wikis (asset-management, naval-architecture, maritime-law, lng-projects, engineering riser, engineering pipeline). The auto-generated `wiki/cross-links.md` files and any faceted-portal pages (#2368 territory) are now stale and need a regeneration pass.

## Why

`scripts/knowledge/wiki-cross-links.py` (#2011) auto-generates per-wiki `cross-links.md` files showing inbound/outbound links across wikis. These files are not git-committed by Tier C agents — they're meant to be refreshed by the script.

Surfaced specifically by vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2587 close-out: the planned `test_asset_management_appears_in_cross_links_md` was rewritten by the implementing agent because:
- `cross-links.md` is auto-generated, not hand-edited
- The agent's scope contract forbade editing files outside its wiki tree
- The test was replaced with a positive inbound-reference assertion on the new pages themselves

The result is that asset-management's `cross-links.md` doesn't yet exist, and the other 5 newly-populated wikis' `cross-links.md` files (where they exist) don't reflect the new pages.

## Scope

1. Run `scripts/knowledge/wiki-cross-links.py` (or its current entry point — verify before running) across all 8 wikis: marine-engineering, engineering, naval-architecture, engineering-standards, asset-management, maritime-law, lng-projects, acma-projects
2. Commit the regenerated `cross-links.md` files
3. Spot-check that the asset-management `cross-links.md` now exists and shows the inbound references from `risk-based-inspection.md`, `fitness-for-service.md`, `integrity-management-cycle.md` to the engineering wiki
4. (Optional, scope decision) If vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#22 faceted-portal generation is wired up, run that too — engineering wiki is now at 103 pages and is the largest target

## Acceptance

- 8 `cross-links.md` files refreshed and committed (or note if any wikis don't yet have one as a deliberate gap)
- Diff reviewable (~bounded by net new pages × link density)
- No test regressions — `tests/knowledge/test_*` stay green

- Faceted-portal authoring (separate scope under vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#22)

## Summary

The 20 new engineering-wiki concept pages added in Tier C Batch C (#2597 risers + vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2602 pipelines, commit `6d3483bc5`) have one-way cross-links to existing related pages but the inbound (reverse) links from those existing pages were intentionally deferred to avoid cross-agent races on shared files during the parallel-dispatch phase.

## Why

Both implementation agents (#2597, vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2602) flagged this in their close-out reports as a known deferral:

- vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2597 deferred the "Related design pages" pointer block on `concepts/viv-riser-fatigue.md`
- vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2602 deferred reverse pointer blocks on `concepts/pipeline-integrity-assessment.md` and `concepts/free-span-viv-fatigue.md`

Without the reverse links, navigation from existing established pages to the new specialized sub-domain pages requires the user to know the new pages exist. The cross-link discoverability layer (#2011, vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#35) and the auto-generated `cross-links.md` (script `scripts/knowledge/wiki-cross-links.py`) help, but human-curated reverse anchors on the established hub pages are higher-signal.

## Scope (single-session implementation, ~30 min)

Add a `## Related design pages` block to each of:

1. `knowledge/wikis/engineering/wiki/concepts/viv-riser-fatigue.md`
   - Link to all 10 `riser-*.md` pages (or the navigationally relevant subset: configurations, steel-catenary, top-tensioned, flexible, hybrid-tower, drilling-system, global-analysis-load-cases, soil-interaction)

   - Link to `pipeline-on-bottom-stability.md`, `pipeline-soil-interaction.md`, `pipeline-route-selection.md`, `riser-soil-interaction.md` (the soil/seabed cluster)

- 3 existing pages amended with `## Related design pages` block
