Execute the already-designed external-source Batch Pack 1 so the repo promotes metadata-rich online data APIs and standards portals into wiki-ready stubs for the thin LLM-wiki domains.

## Why
The repo ecosystem review showed a strong imbalance:
- engineering wiki: 83 pages
- naval-architecture wiki: 45 pages
- maritime-law wiki: 22 pages
- marine-engineering wiki: 19,184 pages

At the same time, the repo already has a prepared execution design:
- `docs/reports/llm-wiki-external-source-priority-queue.md` identifies "Online Data APIs & Standards Portals" as P1 / high-ROI / promotable now.
- `docs/reports/llm-wiki-staged-batch-packs.md` defines Batch Pack 1 as a bounded, overnight-safe metadata-first sweep of 40 entries from `data/document-index/online-resource-registry.yaml`.
- The review explicitly says these entries already have enough structured notes that wiki strengthening can happen without source re-download.

This is low-friction wiki expansion work that uses existing registry intelligence instead of re-parsing raw sources.

## Scope
- Execute Batch Pack 1 from the existing priority-queue and staged-pack artifacts.
- Filter `data/document-index/online-resource-registry.yaml` for `type in [data_api, standard_portal]`.
- Group entries by target wiki domain.
- Produce wiki-ready metadata stubs and a report showing where each source should promote.
- Identify entries that are insufficiently documented and split them into follow-on issues rather than silently expanding scope.

## Deliverables
- A concrete execution artifact/report for the 40 API/portal entries.
- Wiki-ready stubs grouped by engineering, marine-engineering, and naval-architecture target domains.
- Duplicate check against existing wiki pages.
- Follow-on issue map for entries that need extra download/auth work.
- Cross-links to related wiki pages and registry entries.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] all currently eligible API/portal entries are triaged through the batch-pack flow
- [ ] each output stub has a clear target wiki domain and provenance reference
- [ ] duplicate targets are identified before promotion
- [ ] insufficient-note entries are explicitly split into follow-on work
- [ ] the run produces a reusable report rather than one-off notes

## Summary
Execute the already-designed external-source Batch Pack 1 so the repo promotes metadata-rich online data APIs and standards portals into wiki-ready stubs for the thin LLM-wiki domains.

## Why
The repo ecosystem review showed a strong imbalance:
- engineering wiki: 83 pages
- naval-architecture wiki: 45 pages
- maritime-law wiki: 22 pages
- marine-engineering wiki: 19,184 pages

At the same time, the repo already has a prepared execution design:
- `docs/reports/llm-wiki-external-source-priority-queue.md` identifies "Online Data APIs & Standards Portals" as P1 / high-ROI / promotable now.
- `docs/reports/llm-wiki-staged-batch-packs.md` defines Batch Pack 1 as a bounded, overnight-safe metadata-first sweep of 40 entries from `data/document-index/online-resource-registry.yaml`.
- The review explicitly says these entries already have enough structured notes that wiki strengthening can happen without source re-download.

This is low-friction wiki expansion work that uses existing registry intelligence instead of re-parsing raw sources.

## Scope
- Execute Batch Pack 1 from the existing priority-queue and staged-pack artifacts.
- Filter `data/document-index/online-resource-registry.yaml` for `type in [data_api, standard_portal]`.
- Group entries by target wiki domain.
- Produce wiki-ready metadata stubs and a report showing where each source should promote.
- Identify entries that are insufficiently documented and split them into follow-on issues rather than silently expanding scope.

## Deliverables
- A concrete execution artifact/report for the 40 API/portal entries.
- Wiki-ready stubs grouped by engineering, marine-engineering, and naval-architecture target domains.
- Duplicate check against existing wiki pages.
- Follow-on issue map for entries that need extra download/auth work.
- Cross-links to related wiki pages and registry entries.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] all currently eligible API/portal entries are triaged through the batch-pack flow
- [ ] each output stub has a clear target wiki domain and provenance reference
- [ ] duplicate targets are identified before promotion
- [ ] insufficient-note entries are explicitly split into follow-on work
- [ ] the run produces a reusable report rather than one-off notes

- Staged batch packs: vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2243
- Download automation: vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1609
- Engineering wiki ingest: vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#34

{"content": "# Issue Planning Workflow — Onboarding Guide and Plan Index

This document is the single onboarding reference for the mandatory issue planning workflow.
All agents (Claude, Codex, Gemini, Hermes) must follow this workflow for every GitHub issue.

## Why Planning Is Mandatory

Historical data shows that agents skipping the planning step produced incorrect implementations, wasted tokens, and created rework. The planning workflow catches problems before implementation begins, when they are cheapest to fix.

- **Plan review** answers: "Is this the right thing to build?"
- **Cross-review** answers: "Was the right thing built correctly?"

Both are required. Neither replaces the other.

## The Workflow (Step by Step)

```
1. INTAKE           — Read issue, classify complexity (T1/T2/T3)
2. RESOURCE INTEL   — Search existing code, standards, documents, prior plans
3. DRAFT PLAN       — Copy template, fill all sections, save to docs/plans/
4. ADVERSARIAL REVIEW — Route to 2+ AI providers; revise if MAJOR verdict
5. POST TO GITHUB   — Comment plan on issue, label status:plan-review
6. HARD STOP        — Wait for user approval (never self-approve)
7. USER APPROVES    — Swap label to status:plan-approved
8. IMPLEMENT        — TDD: tests first, then code, then full suite
9. CLOSE            — Commit, push, post summary, close issue
```

### Step 1: Intake

- Read the full issue body — scope, acceptance criteria, references
- Classify complexity:
  - **T1** (trivial): config, typo, single-file fix — brief plan, still requires approval
  - **T2** (standard): new module, multiple files, tests — full workflow
  - **T3** (complex): multi-module, architecture, standards — full workflow + subagents

### Step 2: Resource Intelligence

Before writing anything, search all available sources. The retrieval contract (#2208) defines minimum requirements by issue class.

**Universal minimum (ALL issues):**
- **Prior plans**: `docs/plans/` directory and this index
- **Existing code**: search relevant repos in affected paths for prior implementations
- **Recent issues**: related open/closed issues that may overlap or conflict
- **Intelligence entry points**: `docs/document-intelligence/README.md` (when available per #2104) or `docs/document-intelligence/data-intelligence-map.md`

**Issue-class-specific additions:**

| Issue class | Labels / triggers | Additional required sources |
|---|---|---|
| **General** | Default (no specific class match) | Universal minimum is sufficient |
| **Engineering** | `cat:engineering`, `cat:engineering-calculations`, `cat:engineering-methodology` | `standards-transfer-ledger.yaml`, `code-registry.yaml`, relevant domain wiki under `knowledge/wikis/`, `online-resource-registry.yaml` |
| **Data Pipeline** | `cat:data-pipeline` | `registry.yaml`, pipeline config, `resource-intelligence-maturity.yaml` |
| **Documentation** | `cat:documentation` | Governance docs in target directory, `CONTROL_PLANE_CONTRACT.md`, durable-vs-transient boundary policy (#2209) |
| **Harness/Infra** | `cat:harness` | `CONTROL_PLANE_CONTRACT.md`, `config/agents/` settings, `.claude/rules/` |
| **Knowledge/Intelligence** | Issues under #2205 tree, or touching `knowledge/`, `docs/document-intelligence/` | Operating model (#2205), sibling contracts (#2207, #2209), accessibility map (#2096), accessibility registry (when available per #2136) |

If classification is ambiguous or unlabeled, default to **General**. If an issue matches multiple classes, consult the **union** of all matching bundles.

**Evidence requirements:**
- ≥3 distinct sources must be listed in the plan's Resource Intelligence Summary (issue body counts as 1)
- Each source must cite a specific file path, issue number, or registry entry
- Each source must state a concrete finding — not vague claims like "searched the repo"
- The Gaps sub-section must list what must be built from scratch

Full retrieval contract specification: `docs/plans/2026-04-11-issue-2208-intelligence-retrieval-contract-for-github-issue-workflows.md`

### Step 3: Draft Plan

1. Copy the template: `docs/plans/_template-issue-plan.md`
2. Save as: `docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-issue-NNN-slug.md`
3. Fill all required sections (see "Required Sections" below)
4. Add a row to the Index table in this file

### Step 4: Adversarial Review

Route the plan to at least 2 other AI providers. Each gives a verdict:
- **APPROVE** — plan is sound
- **MINOR** — small issues, can proceed after fixing
- **MAJOR** — significant issues, must revise and re-review

Save review artifacts to `scripts/review/results/YYYY-MM-DD-plan-NNN-<agent>.md`.

#### Canonical way to run the adversarial wave (#2323)

```bash
scripts/review/plan-review-fanout.sh docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-issue-NNN-slug.md
```

This wraps Claude + Codex + Gemini in parallel under the shared stance contract
at `scripts/review/plan-review-prompt.md`. It writes one per-provider artifact
plus a `-disagreement.md` summarizing verdict splits + per-provider unique
findings. Per-provider invocation shape is tuned to each CLI's known quirks
(Codex and Gemini get INLINE plan body; Claude gets an `@`-path reference;
Gemini runs from `cwd=/tmp` to dodge the `.gemini/agents/*.md` permissionMode
validation bug). Single-provider failure does not abort the other two — the
failing provider's artifact records `UNAVAILABLE`.

Flags:

- `--providers=claude,codex,gemini` — subset of providers (comma-separated).
- `--output-dir=<dir>` — override the default `scripts/review/results/` sink
  (useful for batch / worktree / test runs).

### Step 5: Post and Label

1. Post the completed plan as a GitHub issue comment
2. Apply label: `gh issue edit NNN --add-label "status:plan-review"`
3. **STOP** — do NOT write any implementation code

### Step 6: User Approval

The user (never the implementing agent) approves the plan:
- `gh issue edit NNN --remove-label "status:plan-review" --add-label "status:plan-approved"`
- Creates marker: `.planning/plan-approved/NNN.md`

### Step 7: Implement (TDD)

Only after `status:plan-approved` label exists:
1. Write tests first — confirm they fail
2. Implement minimum code to pass tests
3. Run full test suite — confirm no regressions
4. Self-review against approved plan

### Step 8: Close

- Conventional commit referencing the issue number
- Push to remote
- Post summary comment on issue: what was done, test results, review verdicts
- Close the issue

**Retrieval evidence at closeout** (per #2208 contract):
- The close comment must include a "Sources consumed" line listing intelligence assets that materially informed implementation (≥1 item)
- The close comment should include a "Promotion candidates" line: "none" or specific findings worth promoting from transient (L5) to durable knowledge (L3) per #2209 Section 7

### Retrieval Evidence at Review Time

Adversarial review artifacts (`scripts/review/results/YYYY-MM-DD-plan-NNN-<agent>.md`) should include a Retrieval Adequacy assessment:

| Check | What the reviewer verifies |
|---|---|
| Resource Intelligence Summary non-empty, ≥3 sources | Plan contains adequate evidence |
| Issue-class-specific sources checked | Obvious sources for the issue class were not missed |
| Evidence is specific | Plan cites file paths and concrete findings, not vague claims |

Reviewers should note a retrieval verdict: `adequate` or `insufficient` with specific gaps.

## Batch / Overnight Sessions

When the user is not present:
- Draft plans and label `status:plan-review` — do NOT implement
- Only implement issues already labeled `status:plan-approved`
- User reviews results the next morning

## Status Meanings

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| draft | Plan file exists locally but has not yet completed adversarial review |
| adversarial-reviewed | Frontier-model review passed; ready to post for user review |
| plan-review | Posted to GitHub; waiting for user approval |
| plan-approved | User approved; ready for implementation or batch execution |
| superseded | Replaced by a newer version of the plan |
| completed | Issue implemented and closed |

## Required Sections in Each Plan

Every plan file must include (see `_template-issue-plan.md` for full format):

1. **Resource Intelligence Summary** — evidence contract: ≥3 sources with specific paths/findings, issue-class-appropriate sources, gaps identified (see template and #2208 contract)
2. **Artifact Map** — paths to plan, tests, implementation, review files
3. **Deliverable** — one sentence: what will exist after this issue is done
4. **Pseudocode** — 5-15 lines per function (T2/T3); "trivial" note for T1
5. **Files to Change** — action, path, reason for each file
6. **TDD Test List** — one row per test with name, verification, input, output
7. **Acceptance Criteria** — checkboxes for all verification steps
8. **Adversarial Review Summary** — provider, verdict, key findings
9. **Risks and Open Questions** — what could go wrong, what needs user input
10. **Complexity** — T1, T2, or T3 with justification

## Enforcement

- **PreToolUse hook**: `.claude/hooks/plan-approval-gate.sh` blocks writes without approval marker
- **Pre-commit hook**: `scripts/enforcement/require-plan-approval.sh --strict` blocks commits without approval
- **Labels**: `status:plan-review` (orange) and `status:plan-approved` (green) exist on the repo

## Key References

| Resource | Path |
|---|---|
| Plan template | `docs/plans/_template-issue-plan.md` |
| Planning skill | `.claude/skills/coordination/issue-planning-mode/SKILL.md` |
| Engineering workflow | `.claude/skills/coordination/engineering-issue-workflow/SKILL.md` |
| Hard-stop policy | `docs/standards/HARD-STOP-POLICY.md` |
| Review artifacts | `scripts/review/results/` |

---

issue.body:
## Summary
Define a computable digitalmodel schema for subsea cable, umbilical, and pipeline cross-sections using a family plus layer/component model.

## Why
Offshore wind cables, oil and gas umbilicals, and rigid pipelines cannot be represented by one generic circular section. Cables are layered electrical/thermal/mechanical systems; umbilicals are packed multi-service bundles; pipelines combine pressure pipe, coatings, insulation, concrete weight coating, anodes, and field-joint discontinuities.

## Knowledge anchors
- `knowledge/wikis/marine-engineering/wiki/concepts/subsea-cable-umbilical-cross-sections.md`
- `knowledge/wikis/marine-engineering/wiki/comparisons/offshore-wind-oil-gas-cross-section-assessment.md`

## Proposed scope
- Create a schema for ordered radial layers and packed components.
- Support families:
  - offshore wind inter-array cable
  - offshore wind HVAC/HVDC export cable
  - steel tube / thermoplastic electro-hydraulic umbilical
  - power/optical hybrid umbilical
  - rigid pipeline/flowline with coating/insulation/concrete layers
- Include static vs dynamic duty metadata, provenance, units, material refs, and validation constraints.
- Provide fixtures for a 66 kV inter-array cable, 220 kV HVAC export cable, steel-tube umbilical, and concrete-coated pipeline.

## Acceptance criteria
- Schema fixtures can represent layer/component geometry, material, density, service role, and provenance without hardcoded vendor assumptions.
- Validation catches missing units, negative thickness/diameter, invalid layer order, and unsupported family names.
- Tests are written before implementation and cover cable, umbilical, and pipeline examples.
- Schema remains extensible for flexible-pipe/riser layer mechanics without forcing them into the first implementation.

## Planning note
This is a feature issue. Implementation requires canonical plan, adversarial review, user approval, then TDD execution.

{"issue": {"url": "https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/1962", "title": "FEATURE: Tier-1 Repo Ecosystem Refactoring — audit, plan, execute with Claude Code plan mode", "issue_number": 1962, "body": "## Summary

Systematic refactoring of the workspace-hub repo ecosystem, starting with tier-1 repositories. The goal is to reduce architectural debt, consolidate duplicate patterns, enforce consistent structure, and improve agent navigability across all tier-1 repos.

## Tier-1 Repos (Priority Order)

| # | Repo | Purpose | Maturity | Depends On |
|---|------|---------|----------|------------|
| 1 | `digitalmodel/` | Engineering digital twin (asset integrity, CP, GIS, hydro) | beta | assetutilities |
| 2 | `assetutilities/` | Shared engineering utilities (config, units, calculations) | stable | — |
| 3 | `assethold/` | Asset portfolio financial analysis | beta | assetutilities |
| 4 | `worldenergydata/` | Global energy market data (BSEE, EIA, drilling) | beta | assetutilities |
| 5 | `CAD-DEVELOPMENTS/` | CAD solvers, models, database, utilities | beta | — |
| 6 | `aceengineer-website/` | Consulting website | — | — |
| 7 | `aceengineer-strategy/` | GTM, business strategy | — | — |
| 8 | `sabithaandkrishnaestates/` | SKEstates Inc. business ops | — | — |

## Refactoring Scope

### Phase 1: Audit (analysis-only, no code changes)
- [ ] Run `repo-architecture-analysis` on each tier-1 repo
- [ ] Identify cross-repo duplicate code (especially assetutilities consumers)
- [ ] Map dependency graph (imports, shared configs, data flows)
- [ ] Catalog test coverage per repo (current state)
- [ ] Identify orphaned/dead code, unused modules, oversized files (>400 lines)
- [ ] Score each repo against the Control-Plane Contract (AGENTS.md, provider adapters)
- [ ] Identify skill duplicates across repos (134 known from vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1720 audit)

### Phase 2: Plan (per-repo refactor plans)
- [ ] Generate refactor plan per tier-1 repo with estimated effort
- [ ] Prioritize by: business value × technical debt severity × dependency impact
- [ ] Identify breaking changes and migration paths
- [ ] Define test coverage targets (tier-1 = 85% per pytest.tier1.ini)

### Phase 3: Execute (TDD, incremental, per-repo)
- [ ] Execute refactors repo-by-repo following dependency order (assetutilities first)
- [ ] TDD mandatory — tests before implementation
- [ ] Each repo refactor as a separate sub-issue for tracking

## Execution Strategy: Claude Code Plan Mode (Cloud)

### Claude Code `--permission-mode plan` ("Ultraplan")

Claude Code v2.1.92 supports `--permission-mode plan` which restricts the agent to **read-only analysis and planning** — no file writes, no shell mutations. This is ideal for Phase 1 (Audit) and Phase 2 (Plan).

**Proposed execution:**

```bash
# Phase 1: Audit each tier-1 repo in plan mode (safe, read-only)
claude --permission-mode plan \
  --print \
  --model claude-opus-4-6 \
  --max-budget-usd 5 \
  -p "Audit the repository architecture of digitalmodel/. Analyze: module structure, dependency graph, test coverage, dead code, file sizes >400 lines, AGENTS.md compliance. Output a structured JSON report."

# Phase 2: Generate refactor plan
claude --permission-mode plan \
  --print \
  --model claude-opus-4-6 \
  --max-budget-usd 5 \
  -p "Given the audit report, generate a prioritized refactor plan for digitalmodel/. Include: breaking changes, migration steps, test targets, estimated effort per module."
```

### Cloud Execution Considerations

| Aspect | Status | Notes |
|--------|--------|-------|
| **Claude Code CLI** | Installed (v2.1.92) | Available on ace-linux-1 |
| **Plan mode** | Supported | `--permission-mode plan` — read-only, safe for audit |
| **API-key mode** | Supported | `--bare` + `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for headless/cloud runs |
| **Print mode** | Supported | `-p` / `--print` for non-interactive batch execution |
| **Budget cap** | Supported | `--max-budget-usd` to control spend per run |
| **Cloud sandbox** | Possible | Can run via Hermes `delegate_task` with `acp_command='claude'` |
| **Max subscription** | Claude Max $200/mo | Rate-limited but sufficient for plan-mode audit |

### Recommended Approach
1. **Phase 1 + 2 (Audit + Plan)**: Run Claude Code in plan mode via `delegate_task(acp_command='claude')` — subagents get isolated context, read-only, budget-capped
2. **Phase 3 (Execute)**: Requires interactive Claude Code sessions with full permissions — NOT suited for autonomous cloud execution without user oversight

## Adversarial Review Requirements

Per [AI Review Routing Policy](docs/standards/AI_REVIEW_ROUTING_POLICY.md):

- **3-agent adversarial review at BOTH stages** (plan + code/artifact)
- Claude: orchestrator + reviewer
- Codex: implementation worker + adversarial reviewer
- Gemini: architecture reviewer + adversarial reviewer
- Max 3 review iterations per deliverable
- All MAJOR findings must be resolved before completion

### Review Checkpoints
1. **After Phase 1 (Audit)**: All 3 agents review the audit findings
2. **After Phase 2 (Plan)**: All 3 agents review each repo's refactor plan
3. **After Phase 3 (Execute)**: All 3 agents review code changes per repo

## Related Issues
- vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1567 — Feature: Continuous Repo Architecture Intelligence
- vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1545 — Agentic feature progression for repo ecosystem productivity under GSD
- vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1603 — Multi-repo architecture scan — expand scanner to all tier-1 repos
- vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1720 — Cross-agent session corpus audit (134 duplicate skills identified)
- vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1734 — chore: add domain skills to assethold (tier-1 with 0 skills)
- vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1661 — Architecture scanner: dependency cycle detection and layering violations
- vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#113 — ROADMAP: Repo ecosystem 3-6 month horizon

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Audit report generated for each tier-1 repo
- [ ] Refactor plan per repo reviewed and approved by all 3 agents
- [ ] Phase 3 sub-issues created with clear scope per repo
- [ ] Test coverage meets tier-1 target (85%) after refactoring
- [ ] Zero cross-repo duplicate skills remaining
- [ ] All repos score 100% on Control-Plane Contract compliance
- [ ] Dependency graph documented and validated

issue.body:
## Context

As part of the Tier-1 Repo Ecosystem Refactoring (#1962), the audit found worldenergydata has 5 failing tests that must be resolved before any refactoring can proceed safely.

## Current State

- Total tests: 431 (5 errors detected during collection)
- Command: `cd assetutilities && uv run python -m pytest ../worldenergydata/tests/ --noconftest` (or run from worldenergydata root)

## Failing Tests

Run `cd /mnt/local-analysis/workspace-hub/worldenergydata && uv run python -m pytest tests/ -v 2>&1 | grep FAILED` to identify exact failures.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 431 tests pass with 0 errors
- [ ] No test regressions
- [ ] Commits follow TDD convention

{"issue": {"url": "https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2005", "title": "audit(digitalmodel): worldenergydata test collection timeout + 14K bytecode files — investigate and resolve", "issue_number": 2005, "body": "## Context

Tier-1 Repo Audit (#1962) found critical infrastructure issues in worldenergydata:

### Test Collection Timeout
- The test suite times out during collection (>30s)
- Cannot even enumerate tests, let alone run them
- Likely caused by heavy imports or expensive fixture setup

### 14,145 Bytecode Files
- Extremely deep dependency tree
- 11.71s compile time — major code smell
- May indicate excessive dependencies in pyproject.toml
- Consider lazy imports or splitting dev dependencies

## Investigation Steps

1. `uv run python -c "import time; start=time.time(); import worldenergydata; print(f'import took {time.time()-start:.2f}s')"`
2. Audit pyproject.toml — check for unnecessary dev dependencies being installed
3. Profile imports: `python -X importtime -m worldenergydata 2>&1 | tail -50`
4. Identify which 14K .pyc files belong to which packages

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test collection completes within 30s
- [ ] All 431 tests pass with 0 errors
- [ ] Bytecode file count explained or reduced
- [ ] pyproject.toml cleaned if needed

{"issue": {"url": "https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2006", "title": "audit(worldenergydata): 14000+ orphan modules — triage for archival vs active use (#1962 Phase 3)", "issue_number": 2006, "body": "## Context

Tier-1 Repo Audit (#1962) identified **10+ orphan modules** in worldenergydata (files with 0 imports).

## Orphan Detection Method

The audit used grep-based import counting — a weak heuristic that misses dynamic imports, __import__(), and importlib usage. So the true orphan count may be lower.

## Work

1. Run AST-based orphan detection (proper import analysis)
2. For each confirmed orphan: check if it's a CLI entry point (not imported but executed)
3. Archive truly unused modules or mark with `# CLI entry point` header
4. Update documentation accordingly

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AST-based orphan scan complete
- [ ] All orphans categorized (archive / CLI / dynamic import / keep)
- [ ] Unused code archived with clear git history

## Context

Tier-1 Repo Audit (#1962) identified **10+ orphan modules** in worldenergydata (files with 0 imports).

## Orphan Detection Method

The audit used grep-based import counting — a weak heuristic that misses dynamic imports, __import__(), and importlib usage. So the true orphan count may be lower.

## Work

1. Run AST-based orphan detection (proper import analysis)
2. For each confirmed orphan: check if it's a CLI entry point (not imported but executed)
3. Archive truly unused modules or mark with `# CLI entry point` header
4. Update documentation accordingly

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AST-based orphan scan complete
- [ ] All orphans categorized (archive / CLI / dynamic import / keep)
- [ ] Unused code archived with clear git history

## Objective
Harden plan-review artifacts so continuous planning reports can reliably distinguish current clean reviews from stale, missing, empty, disagreement-only, or legacy/no-SHA artifacts.

Parent stream: #2489

## Why this matters
#2489 now depends on SHA-bound review evidence before Lane A/B classification. Reusing dated artifact paths across revisions makes stale artifacts easy for humans and scripts to misread.

## Scope
- Define required metadata fields for provider review artifacts: issue, plan path, plan commit, Plan-SHA256, provider/perspective, verdict, timestamp, reviewed revision.
- Add parser behavior for stale prior-SHA artifacts vs no-review-yet vs unavailable provider.
- Define how synthesis/disagreement artifacts relate to provider verdicts without being counted as provider reviews.
- Add tests/fixtures for SHA mismatch, missing SHA, empty artifact, disagreement-only evidence, and stale artifact messaging.

## Out of scope
- Implementing #2489 classifier itself.
- Changing approval-marker semantics.
- Bypassing required providers.

## Acceptance criteria
- Review artifact contract documented and machine-checkable.
- Existing #2489 review-artifact edge cases have deterministic classifications.
- Report messaging makes stale-vs-missing review evidence obvious to operators.

- Define lease_scope normalization for issue/module/file overlaps.
- Propose a separate writer/lock owner implementation path.

## Out of scope
- Launching remote routines in #2489.
- Treating ledger state as approval authority.
- Replacing repo hooks or approval markers.

## Acceptance criteria
- Trusted vs untrusted ledger criteria are deterministic.
- Missing/untrusted ledger cannot produce “safe to dispatch” claims.

{"issue": {"url": "https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2518", "title": "fix(review): harden plan-review fanout provider invocation", "issue_number": 2518, "body": "## Summary
Post-reboot recovery of the wave-2/wave-3 adversarial plan-review batch exposed provider-wrapper failures in `scripts/review/plan-review-fanout.sh`. The review fanout repeatedly produced `UNAVAILABLE` or empty provider artifacts rather than canonical `APPROVE|MINOR|MAJOR` review artifacts.

## Evidence from recovery
- Worktree: `/mnt/local-analysis/reconcile-main-20260427`
- Status handoff: `docs/handoffs/2026-04-27-wave2-wave3-review-status.md`
- Affected artifacts: `scripts/review/results/2026-04-27-plan-*-{claude,codex,gemini}.md`
- Gemini failures show rc=55: workspace trust is not configured. Future invocations likely need `GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true` or `--skip-trust`.
- Codex runs emitted useful session output to `.err` while canonical `.md` stayed empty or was replaced with `UNAVAILABLE`; wrapper should normalize stdout/stderr capture and only mark failed after checking both.
- Claude/fanout processes hung/stalled during post-reboot recovery and needed termination to prevent duplicate spend.

## Desired outcome
Make plan-review fanout robust enough that future review waves produce deterministic artifacts:
1. Per-provider timeout and process-group cleanup.
2. Gemini trusted-workspace handling from noninteractive runs.
3. Codex stdout/stderr normalization and no stdin wait.
4. Explicit `UNAVAILABLE` stubs only when a provider truly failed, with actionable reason.
5. A status summary that distinguishes `PENDING`, `UNAVAILABLE`, and real review verdicts.

## Acceptance criteria
- Reproduce and fix the Gemini rc=55 trust failure in noninteractive fanout.
- Reproduce and fix Codex canonical artifact loss when output is emitted through stderr/session stream.
- Add tests or a dry-run harness proving empty provider outputs are converted to actionable stubs and do not silently pass.
- Re-run a small representative plan-review batch and verify artifacts include canonical sections: `Verdict`, `Retrieval`, `Findings`, `Blockers`.
- Do not auto-approve any plans as part of this infra fix.

## Related
- Recovery handoff: `docs/handoffs/2026-04-27-wave2-wave3-review-status.md`
- Review script: `scripts/review/plan-review-fanout.sh`

{"issue": {"url": "https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2489", "title": "feat(ai-orchestration): continuous planning pipeline for AFK issue throughput", "issue_number": 2489, "body": "## Summary
Build a continuous planning + execution-readiness pipeline so workspace-hub always has a buffer of issues that are:

1. intake-complete,
2. resource-intel complete,
3. repo-tracked plan drafted,
4. adversarially reviewed,
5. waiting for explicit user approval (`status:plan-review`), or already user-approved and implementation-ready (`status:plan-approved` + local approval marker).

The target operating model is day/night throughput similar to Matt Pocock's AFK-agent loop: day shift = plan/review/QA; night shift = bounded AFK implementation/review; morning = user review/QA + approval of the next queue.

Reference idea: https://x.com/mattpocockuk/status/2048159313357598989

## Why
Current workflow has strong gates, but the queue can still starve:

- Implementation stalls if too few issues are `status:plan-approved` with local markers.
- Planning stalls if there is no ranked plan-review/pre-plan backlog.
- Morning user review is less efficient if yesterday's agents did not prepare a focused approval shortlist.
- Overnight Claude work should not improvise scope; it should continuously pull from pre-planned, reviewed, user-approved work or generate approval-ready plans for the next day.

## Desired operating model
Maintain three always-visible lanes:

### Lane A — approval candidates
Issues with canonical plan + valid adversarial review + no MAJOR blockers, ready for user approve/revise/reject.

### Lane B — execution-ready
Issues with `status:plan-approved`, canonical plan, and committed `.planning/plan-approved/<issue>.md` marker; safe for overnight implementation waves.

### Lane C — planning feedstock
High-value open issues without plan artifacts, ranked for the next planning-only batch.

The pipeline should keep target buffers, for example:

- 5-10 issues in Lane A for morning user review.
- 5-10 issues in Lane B for overnight implementation.
- 10-20 issues in Lane C for continuous planning.

## Scope
Create a repo-owned operational mechanism for this continuous pipeline.

Expected deliverables may include:

- A documented day/night operating contract under `docs/standards/` or `docs/plans/`.
- A queue audit/report command or script that classifies issues into Lane A/B/C using live GitHub state plus local plan/review/approval-marker artifacts.
- A morning review pack artifact that lists the exact issues the user should review/approve and why.
- An overnight dispatch pack artifact that lists implementation-ready issues and zero-overlap workstream boundaries.
- Guardrails that prevent stale labels from being treated as sufficient approval.
- Follow-up issue creation for blockers/deferred scope discovered during planning and QA.

## Acceptance criteria
- Running the pipeline audit produces a current Lane A/B/C report with clickable GitHub issue links.
- The report verifies all approval surfaces, not labels alone:
  - GitHub `status:*` label,
  - canonical `docs/plans/...issue-NNN...md` plan,
  - review artifacts / synthesis,
  - `.planning/plan-approved/NNN.md` marker for execution-ready issues.
- The report explicitly distinguishes:
  - ready for user approval,
  - approved and execution-ready,
  - needs plan work,
  - blocked / stale / review failed.
- A morning operator can approve/revise/reject a focused shortlist without re-triaging the entire backlog.
- An overnight operator can launch planning-only or implementation-only waves without violating plan gates or causing git contention.
- The mechanism includes adversarial review at both plan-review and code/artifact-review stages.

## Related existing issues / surfaces
- #1839 — Workflow hard-stops and session governance.
- #2129 — Automate issue-state drift and redundancy audit.
- #2255 — Reconcile GitHub plan-approval labels with local marker ledger.
- Existing `gh-work-planning` and overnight prompt workflows.

## Notes from referenced X thread
The useful pattern is not "let agents code all night unbounded." It is:

- Day shift: requirements, PRD/issues, plan/review, QA.
- Night shift: planner identifies unblocked work, launches sandboxed implementation agents, runs reviewer agents, creates PRs/branches, then loops.
- Morning/day QA: review branches, create follow-ups, adjust destination, and refill the queue.

For workspace-hub, this must be adapted to the stricter hard-stop policy: no implementation before plan review + user approval + local marker evidence.

- A queue audit/report command or script that classifies issues into Lane A/B/C using live GitHub state plus local plan/review/approval-marker artifacts.
- A morning review pack artifact that lists the exact issues the user should review/approve and why.
- An overnight dispatch pack artifact that lists implementation-ready issues and zero-overlap workstream boundaries.
- Guardrails that prevent stale labels from being treated as sufficient approval.
- Follow-up issue creation for blockers/deferred scope discovered during planning and QA.

## Acceptance criteria
- Running the pipeline audit produces a current Lane A/B/C report with clickable GitHub issue links.
- The report verifies all approval surfaces, not labels alone:
  - GitHub `status:*` label,
  - canonical `docs/plans/...issue-NNN...md` plan,
  - review artifacts / synthesis,
  - `.planning/plan-approved/NNN.md` marker for execution-ready issues.
- The report explicitly distinguishes:
  - ready for user approval,
  - approved and execution-ready,
  - needs plan work,
  - blocked / stale / review failed.
- A morning operator can approve/revise/reject a focused shortlist without re-triaging the entire backlog.
- An overnight operator can launch planning-only or implementation-only waves without violating plan gates or causing git contention.
- The mechanism includes adversarial review at both plan-review and code/artifact-review stages.

## Related existing issues / surfaces
- #1839 — Workflow hard-stops and session governance.
- #2129 — Automate issue-state drift and redundancy audit.
- #2255 — Reconcile GitHub plan-approval labels with local marker ledger.
- Existing `gh-work-planning` and overnight prompt workflows.

## Notes from referenced X thread
The useful pattern is not "let agents code all night unbounded." It is:

- Day shift: requirements, PRD/issues, plan/review, QA.
- Night shift: planner identifies unblocked work, launches sandboxed implementation agents, runs reviewer agents, creates PRs/branches, then loops.
- Morning/day QA: review branches, create follow-ups, adjust destination, and refill the queue.

For workspace-hub, this must be adapted to the stricter hard-stop policy: no implementation before plan review + user approval + local marker evidence.

# Swarm 4 — Execution-Readiness Partition

Date: 2026-05-10
Scope: planning-only backlog partition for independent future AI-agent workstreams.
Write boundary for this audit: `docs/plans/agent-swarm-audits/2026-05-10/swarm-4-execution-readiness-partition.md` only.

No implementation was launched. No labels, issues, approval markers, source files, tests, or other swarm-owned audit files were changed.

## Backlog partition summary

Result: 5 candidate future lanes exist, but 0 lanes are currently classified as execution-ready under the strict gate.

Reason: current live issue evidence contains several promising `status:plan-approved` labels, but the execution gate requires more than labels. The planning workflow requires a canonical plan, adversarial review, user approval, and committed local approval marker evidence before implementation. Where approval evidence is incomplete, stale, contradicted, blocked, or not locally verifiable, the lane is classified as planning-only, approval-needed, or blocked rather than executable.

Conservative classification summary:

| Lane | Theme | Candidate posture | Execution-ready? | Why not executable now |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| A | Governance / issue-plan cleanup | approval-needed | no | Multiple governance issues are draft/no-label or explicitly decision-needed; some have live label ambiguity without marker evidence. |
| B | Docs / mission contracts | approval-needed | no | Mission/repo-structure items include plan-approved labels, but local marker evidence was not verified; some plan index evidence contradicts issue label state. |
| C | Engineering-domain readiness | blocked / approval-needed | no | Engineering items are blocked, closed, or missing canonical approval evidence; solver-ready items require local host validation and marker checks. |
| D | GTM / demo artifact readiness | planning-only | no | April vessel GTM issues are mostly closed; future GTM packaging should start from a new bounded plan or explicit continuation issue. |
| E | Knowledge / skill / llm-wiki pipeline | approval-needed / blocked | no | llm-wiki batch parents are approved but blocked by missing public-safe inputs; prep issues are at plan-review, not approved. |
